content.text:
# Daily auto-publish (issue #161): thin orchestrator over the existing
# publish channels. Each channel is an isolated leg — one leg failing never
# kills the others — and every failure self-files a deduplicated GitHub
# issue (label `bug`, assigned to the owner) that auto-closes when the leg
# goes green again. No publish logic is duplicated here: legs dispatch the
# existing workflows via `gh workflow run` and watch them.
#
#   testflight  build-mobile.yml   ios_content=all (the iOS half of the
#                                 mobile build)
#   play        build-mobile.yml   android_content=all,
#                                 android_track=beta (Android external
#                                 beta / open testing — issue #289 lifts
#                                 the standing "Android excluded" owner
#                                 decision for the release track; #947
#                                 adds the listing deploy — texts +
#                                 whole-set image replace + verify — so
#                                 the listing never trails the goldens;
#                                 the leg green-skips while the Play
#                                 secrets are absent)
#   pubdev      in-job OIDC publish, only when pubspec > pub.dev; otherwise
#               a green up-to-date check. The tag-time OIDC publish job
#               (ci.yml) stays the primary path; this leg is the catch-up +
#               loud-failure detector (e.g. expired publish credentials)
#   cli         build-macos.yml    desktop DMG + macOS CLI bundles +
#                                 extension, attached to the next-tag
#                                 release (version passed explicitly so
#                                 mobile/desktop never mint diverging tags)
#   windows     build-windows.yml windows-x64 app zip (fa-app-windows-x64.zip,
#                                 stable name), attached to the next-tag
#                                 release — the Windows counterpart of the
#                                 TestFlight leg: one release-quality GUI
#                                 app build per day (gh-2140)
#   website     pages.yml          fa1.dev (landing + web demo +
#                                 the /outlook add-in slice; gh-1684:
#                                 the extension zip moved to GitHub
#                                 Releases and is no longer site-hosted)
#   addin       office-addin.yml   manifest/taskpane acceptance suite; the
#                                 fa1.dev publish itself rides the website
#                                 leg (pages.yml assembles /outlook)
#
# Legs run only when main moved since the last GREEN daily run — skip-no-
# change is green-neutral, never red (#159 lesson). One exception (gh-1192):
# while main's pubspec version is not yet served by pub.dev the plan gate
# (scripts/daily_plan.sh) forces the legs anyway — a release-in-flight
# green must not become a skip baseline that stalls re-verification and
# rerun-recovery on a quiet main. Versioning stays the
# existing scheme: auto_release.sh patch-bumps + tags every main push
# (2h coalesce); the daily attaches mobile/desktop artifacts to the next
# tag and verifies/republishes pub.dev. See docs/ci.md.
#
# Pause: gh workflow disable daily-publish.yml -R IstiN/flutter_agent_harness

name: Daily auto-publish

run-name: "Daily auto-publish (${{ inputs.legs || 'all' }})"

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '17 5 * * *' # once daily, 05:17 UTC
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      legs:
        description: 'Leg(s) to run'
        type: choice
        default: all
        options:
          - all
          - testflight
          - play
          - pubdev
          - cli
          - windows
          - website
          - addin
      force:
        description: 'Run even if main has not moved since the last green daily'
        type: boolean
        default: false
      inject_failure:
        description: 'TEST ONLY — fail this leg before any dispatch, to exercise the self-filing issue cycle'
        type: choice
        default: none
        options:
          - none
          - testflight
          - play
          - pubdev
          - cli
          - windows
          - website
          - addin

permissions:
  contents: read

# One daily at a time; a queued run must not cancel an in-flight one.
concurrency:
  group: daily-publish
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  plan:
    name: Plan (change detection + versions)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # gh-1477: 10m was the same time bomb as the derive-version jobs — a
    # full-history fetch under a 10m ceiling. 20m + the blobless filter
    # below.
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: read
    outputs:
      changed: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.changed }}
      next_tag: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.next_tag }}
      latest_tag: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.latest_tag }}
      pubspec_version: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.pubspec_version }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # gh-1477: daily_plan.sh reads tags / commit metadata / one file
          # at origin/main — never historical blobs. Blobless keeps full
          # tag/commit metadata without the blobs (the full fetch outgrew
          # the old 10m ceiling in the twin derive-version job, run
          # 38027695551).
          fetch-depth: 0
          filter: blob:none

      - name: Detect main movement and derive versions
        id: plan
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          FORCE: ${{ inputs.force }}
        # gh-1192: the gate (baseline + the release-unresolved re-arm that
        # keeps AC1's «the next daily re-verifies» true on a quiet main)
        # lives in the extracted script — shell-harness tested by
        # test/release_flow_race_test.dart.
        run: bash scripts/daily_plan.sh

  # ── Dispatch legs ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Shape per leg: dispatch the child workflow pinned to main, capture the
  # new run id, wait for it read-only, fail on any non-success conclusion.
  # The child run URL is exported even on failure so the report can excerpt
  # its log.
  #
  # ── The gh-1903 invariant: queued on the single self-hosted runner is
  # HEALTHY ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # dispatch_and_watch.sh NEVER cancels or re-dispatches a child mid-watch.
  # A child queued behind siblings on the shared fa-m5-1 is normal
  # operation; the old #344 budget + gh-172 queue-stall watchdog cancelled
  # two such healthy queued children on 2026-10-26 (daily run 40274465122,
  # tracking issue #1735 — those cancellations were THIS defect, not an
  # ASC/IPA problem) and failed a fully-built v1.0.648 solely by killing
  # its place in line. What bounds a slow child instead:
  #   * every job in a watched child chain carries an explicit
  #     timeout-minutes — a wedged self-hosted job self-fails server-side
  #     (#344; a job-level timeout is enforced BY the runner, which is why
  #     a hung worker outliving its own ceiling is the one class the
  #     server cannot kill), and
  #   * the leg timeout-minutes below — when it fires, the runner TERMs
  #     the watcher, which cancels ONLY this leg's own NEVER-STARTED child
  #     (gh-1903 orphan-cancel) so an orphaned queued run cannot publish
  #     unattended, then fails naming the child run, its last observed
  #     state, and the observed pool activity (gh-172 diagnostic).
  # While the child has not started, the watcher logs sibling in-progress
  # runs on a diagnostic interval — read-only; cannot-observe ⇒
  # cannot-judge ⇒ never a cancel.
  #
  # ── Timeout arithmetic (#351, leg-timeout sizing) ────────────────────────
  # Child worst-case = sum of the serialized job timeout-minutes along the
  # child's critical path (every job in a watched chain carries an explicit
  # timeout for exactly this). Invariant: leg timeout > child worst-case +
  # margin (appear window 60×10s ≈ 10m + poll slack ≈ 5m) — the leg always
  # outlives a healthy slow child, which is now NEVER killed.
  #
  #   leg        child worst-case (serialized chain)          leg timeout
  #   testflight version 20 → build-ios 90 → submit-ios 120   230m  ;  360m
  #             (∥ release-mobile 15, covered by the max)
  #   play       version 20 → build-android 45 →              95m   ;  240m
  #             submit-android 30 (∥ release-mobile 15)
  #   cli        version 20 → build-macos 150×2 (arm64 +      335m  ;  360m
  #             x86_64 SERIALIZE on the single self-hosted
  #             runner) → release-macos 15
  #             (∥ cli matrix 45, extension 30 — shorter paths)
  #   (gh-1477: the version/plan jobs' ceiling moved 10 → 20m — a
  #   full-history fetch outgrew the 10m bomb; the fetch is now blobless
  #   and 20m is the seatbelt. Worst-cases grew by exactly the +10m.)
  #   website    pages build 45 → deploy 15                   60m   ;  180m
  #   addin      office-addin-suite 45 (single job)           45m   ;  150m
  #
  # gh-172 (run 39374894901, 2026-10-20) history: the re-dispatched
  # testflight child sat queued FOREVER on the zombie self-hosted worker —
  # the leg burned its remaining ~107m and died as a bare 360m ceiling
  # kill with no diagnosis. The budget/stall watchdog built to catch that
  # faster could not tell a zombie-held pool from a sibling leg's job
  # legitimately occupying the shared fa-m5-1 (its own comment admitted
  # it), and its 31m stall window did not cover the cli sibling chain's
  # 335m worst-case — so it false-cancelled healthy queues by design
  # (gh-1903, #1735). The zombie goal is now met by the bounds above plus
  # the leg-timeout orphan-cancel diagnostic, not by a heuristic that
  # cannot tell a queue from a zombie.

  testflight:
    name: 'Leg: TestFlight'
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # #351 arithmetic: child wc 230m (version 20 + build-ios 90 +
    # submit-ios 120); 360m leg > worst-case + ~15m margin. The 360m cap
    # also bounds any gh-172 zombie wait — on leg timeout the watcher's
    # orphan-cancel kills only this leg's never-started child (gh-1903).
    timeout-minutes: 360
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: write
    if: >-
      (needs.plan.outputs.changed == 'true' || inputs.force == true) &&
      (inputs.legs == '' || inputs.legs == 'all' || inputs.legs == 'testflight')
    outputs:
      run_url: ${{ steps.dispatch.outputs.run_url }}
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Inject failure (test)
        if: inputs.inject_failure == 'testflight'
        run: |
          echo "::error::injected failure (inject_failure=testflight) — exercising the self-filing issue path, nothing dispatched"
          exit 1

      - name: Dispatch build-mobile.yml and watch
        id: dispatch
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Shared watcher (gh-1903, correlation from #343): correlates
          # OUR run by the child's run-name ("build-mobile (none/all)" —
          # displayTitle is the only distinguisher in the run-list API),
          # newest match in a tight window. Waits READ-ONLY: a child
          # queued behind siblings on the shared fa-m5-1 is healthy and is
          # never cancelled/re-dispatched; the bounds are build-ios/
          # submit-ios's own timeout-minutes (#344) and this leg's 360m.
          # On leg timeout the watcher cancels only this leg's own
          # never-started orphan child (gh-1903) — see the leg-header
          # comment for the full invariant.
          rc=0
          bash scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh build-mobile.yml \
            --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --ref main \
            --title 'build-mobile (none/all)' \
            -f android_content=none -f ios_content=all \
            --out-run-id run_id.txt || rc=$?
          if [ -s run_id.txt ]; then
            echo "run_url=https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/$(cat run_id.txt)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          exit "$rc"

  play:
    name: 'Leg: Play (Android external beta)'
    # Independent of the testflight leg (#359). The #348 serialization was
    # a mitigation for the #343 sibling-dispatch race; #351 eliminated that
    # race structurally — exact displayTitle correlation (this leg's child
    # runs as "build-mobile (all/none)", the testflight leg's as
    # "(none/all)"), NEWEST match, a tight 30s window, and build-mobile's
    # per-run_id concurrency group (no dispatch can cancel another). With
    # the race gone the needs-edge only bought harm: a cancelled testflight
    # watcher skipped Play behind it and the edge added up to 360m of start
    # latency (one leg's external blocker stopped the train — run
    # 34827074052, BETA_REVIEW_CONTACT_EMAIL user-owned).
    #
    # The two residual #346 concerns are handled structurally, not by
    # ordering:
    #   * same-tag convergence — both children independently derive
    #     latest-tag+1, so they can attach to ONE release concurrently;
    #     release_attach_or_create.sh is race-idempotent (a lost create
    #     uploads into the winner's release) with an ownership-scoped draft
    #     guard, and the asset sets never collide (AAB vs IPA).
    #   * runner contention — none: the Android chain is all GitHub-hosted
    #     runners; only build-ios touches the single self-hosted macOS
    #     runner (which already serializes physically with the cli leg's
    #     build-macos children — that pair has always been independent).
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # #351 arithmetic (unchanged by #359 — only the leg's START moved):
    # child wc 95m (version 20 + build-android 45 + submit-android 30);
    # 240m leg > worst-case + ~15m margin. Waits are read-only (gh-1903) —
    # no cancel, no re-dispatch, bounded by the child's per-job timeouts
    # (#344) and this leg timeout.
    timeout-minutes: 240
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: write
    if: >-
      (needs.plan.outputs.changed == 'true' || inputs.force == true) &&
      (inputs.legs == '' || inputs.legs == 'all' || inputs.legs == 'play')
    outputs:
      run_url: ${{ steps.dispatch.outputs.run_url }}
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
      # Secrets presence is checked in the first step — while the Play
      # upload keystore/service account are not configured, the leg green-
      # skips with a notice (existing neutral-skip leg semantics); it goes
      # live the moment the owner sets them (issue #289).
      PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON: ${{ secrets.PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON }}
      ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64 }}
      ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD }}
      ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS }}
      ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Inject failure (test)
        if: inputs.inject_failure == 'play'
        run: |
          echo "::error::injected failure (inject_failure=play) — exercising the self-filing issue path, nothing dispatched"
          exit 1

      - name: Skip without Play secrets (green-neutral)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          missing=""
          [ -z "${ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64:-}" ] && missing="$missing ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64"
          [ -z "${ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD:-}" ] && missing="$missing ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD"
          [ -z "${ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS:-}" ] && missing="$missing ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS"
          [ -z "${ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD:-}" ] && missing="$missing ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD"
          if [ -z "${PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON:-}" ]; then
            missing="$missing PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON"
          fi
          if [ -n "$missing" ]; then
            echo "::notice::Play secrets not configured (missing:${missing}) — the Android leg skips green-neutrally until the upload keystore + Play service account secrets exist (issue #289 owner checklist)."
            exit 0
          fi
          echo "All Play secrets present — dispatching the Android build+upload."

      - name: Dispatch build-mobile.yml and watch
        id: dispatch
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # all: build + Play upload + LISTING deploy (issue #947) — the
          # listing lane replaces the whole image set per locale + device
          # type and verifies it via edits.images.list, so the listing can
          # never trail the committed goldens by more than one train.
          # beta = the external/open testing track, mirroring the iOS leg's
          # external TestFlight group (#239 pattern).
          # Shared watcher (gh-1903 read-only wait; correlation from #343).
          # Since #359 the TestFlight
          # sibling leg fires CONCURRENTLY with this one (both needs: plan)
          # and dispatches the SAME workflow in the same minute —
          # correlation is by the child's run-name ("build-mobile
          # (all/none)" vs the sibling's "(none/all)", pinned by
          # test), never by "first run in the window", with newest-match +
          # the 30s window. Read-only wait (gh-1903): a wedged/queued run
          # is NEVER cancelled or re-dispatched — build-android/submit-
          # android's own timeout-minutes (#344) and this leg's 240m are
          # the only bounds; on leg timeout only this leg's own
          # never-started orphan child is cancelled.
          rc=0
          bash scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh build-mobile.yml \
            --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --ref main \
            --title 'build-mobile (all/none)' \
            -f android_content=all -f android_track=beta -f ios_content=none \
            --out-run-id run_id.txt || rc=$?
          if [ -s run_id.txt ]; then
            echo "run_url=https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/$(cat run_id.txt)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          exit "$rc"

  cli:
    name: 'Leg: CLI + macOS desktop'
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # #351 arithmetic: child wc 335m (version 20 + build-macos 150×2 — the
    # arm64 AND x86_64 matrix legs SERIALIZE on the single self-hosted
    # macOS runner — + release-macos 15); 360m leg ≥ worst-case + margin
    # (both build-macos jobs carry 150m server-side timeouts, #344). A
    # queued child — including one waiting out a sibling's full 150m
    # matrix leg — is NEVER cancelled (gh-1903); the leg timeout bounds
    # the wait and the watcher orphan-cancels only a never-started child.
    timeout-minutes: 360
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: write
    if: >-
      (needs.plan.outputs.changed == 'true' || inputs.force == true) &&
      (inputs.legs == '' || inputs.legs == 'all' || inputs.legs == 'cli')
    outputs:
      run_url: ${{ steps.dispatch.outputs.run_url }}
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Inject failure (test)
        if: inputs.inject_failure == 'cli'
        run: |
          echo "::error::injected failure (inject_failure=cli) — exercising the self-filing issue path, nothing dispatched"
          exit 1

      - name: Dispatch build-macos.yml and watch
        id: dispatch
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Children derive version themselves (latest tag + 1 at their own
          # dispatch moment) — a tag pinned here would race auto_release and
          # could attach assets to a tag pointing at a different commit.
          # Shared watcher (gh-1903 read-only wait; correlation from #343):
          # correlates OUR run by the child's run-name
          # ("build-macos (create_release=true)") so a concurrent human
          # dispatch is never adopted. A wedged self-hosted run is NEVER
          # cancelled/re-dispatched — the bounds are the build-macos jobs'
          # own 150m server-side timeouts (#344) and this leg's 360m; on
          # leg timeout the watcher orphan-cancels only this leg's own
          # never-started child.
          rc=0
          bash scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh build-macos.yml \
            --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --ref main \
            --title 'build-macos (create_release=true)' \
            -f create_release=true \
            --out-run-id run_id.txt || rc=$?
          if [ -s run_id.txt ]; then
            echo "run_url=https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/$(cat run_id.txt)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          exit "$rc"

  windows:
    name: 'Leg: Windows app'
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # #351 arithmetic: child wc 85m (version 20 + windows build 45 +
    # attach 20); 150m leg > worst-case + margin (the addin-leg sizing).
    timeout-minutes: 150
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: write
    if: >-
      (needs.plan.outputs.changed == 'true' || inputs.force == true) &&
      (inputs.legs == '' || inputs.legs == 'all' || inputs.legs == 'windows')
    outputs:
      run_url: ${{ steps.dispatch.outputs.run_url }}
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Inject failure (test)
        if: inputs.inject_failure == 'windows'
        run: |
          exit 1

      - name: Dispatch build-windows.yml and watch
        id: dispatch
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # The child derives the version itself (same latest-tag+1 math as
          # build-macos/build-mobile — all release children derive the SAME
          # next tag). Shared watcher (gh-1903): correlates OUR run by the
          # child's run-name, waits READ-ONLY within the child's own
          # timeout bounds, orphan-cancels only this leg's never-started
          # child on leg timeout.
          rc=0
          bash scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh build-windows.yml \
            --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --ref main \
            --title 'build-windows (create_release=true)' \
            -f create_release=true \
            --out-run-id run_id.txt || rc=$?
          if [ -s run_id.txt ]; then
            echo "run_url=https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/$(cat run_id.txt)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          exit "$rc"

  website:
    name: 'Leg: Website'
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # #351 arithmetic: child wc 60m (pages build 45 + deploy 15); 180m leg
    # ≫ worst-case + margin. (The old 45m leg pre-dated #351 and could not
    # even fit a healthy child + appear window — the 180m leg is the
    # #351 sizing.)
    timeout-minutes: 180
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: write
    if: >-
      (needs.plan.outputs.changed == 'true' || inputs.force == true) &&
      (inputs.legs == '' || inputs.legs == 'all' || inputs.legs == 'website')
    outputs:
      run_url: ${{ steps.dispatch.outputs.run_url }}
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Inject failure (test)
        if: inputs.inject_failure == 'website'
        run: |
          echo "::error::injected failure (inject_failure=website) — exercising the self-filing issue path, nothing dispatched"
          exit 1

      # pages.yml is path-filtered on push, so routine pushes (e.g. lib/
      # changes outside its filters) never redeploy — the daily guarantees
      # fa1.dev tracks main.
      - name: Dispatch pages.yml and watch
        id: dispatch
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Shared watcher (gh-1903 read-only wait; correlation from #343).
          # pages.yml takes no inputs, so there is no displayTitle to
          # disambiguate on — the watcher falls back to
          # newest-in-tight-window and waits read-only: no cancel, no
          # re-dispatch, bounded by the pages jobs' own timeout-minutes
          # (#344) and this leg's 180m.
          rc=0
          bash scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh pages.yml \
            --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --ref main \
            --out-run-id run_id.txt || rc=$?
          if [ -s run_id.txt ]; then
            echo "run_url=https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/$(cat run_id.txt)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          exit "$rc"

  addin:
    name: 'Leg: Outlook add-in'
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # #351 arithmetic: child wc 45m (single office-addin-suite job); 150m
    # leg ≫ worst-case + margin. (The old 45m leg pre-dated #351 and could
    # not even fit a healthy child + appear window — 150m is the #351
    # sizing.)
    timeout-minutes: 150
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: write
    if: >-
      (needs.plan.outputs.changed == 'true' || inputs.force == true) &&
      (inputs.legs == '' || inputs.legs == 'all' || inputs.legs == 'addin')
    outputs:
      run_url: ${{ steps.dispatch.outputs.run_url }}
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Inject failure (test)
        if: inputs.inject_failure == 'addin'
        run: |
          echo "::error::injected failure (inject_failure=addin) — exercising the self-filing issue path, nothing dispatched"
          exit 1

      # Acceptance suite (manifest validation, dart2js taskpane, Node +
      # Playwright e2e). The fa1.dev /outlook publish itself rides the
      # website leg — pages.yml assembles the same add-in into the deploy.
      - name: Dispatch office-addin.yml and watch
        id: dispatch
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Shared watcher (gh-1903 read-only wait; correlation from #343).
          # No inputs to disambiguate on (newest-in-tight-window
          # fallback); the wait is bounded by the office-addin-suite
          # job's own 45m timeout (#344) and this leg's 150m — never by a
          # watcher cancel.
          rc=0
          bash scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh office-addin.yml \
            --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --ref main \
            --out-run-id run_id.txt || rc=$?
          if [ -s run_id.txt ]; then
            echo "run_url=https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/$(cat run_id.txt)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          exit "$rc"

  # ── pub.dev leg ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # The ONLY publish path is the ci.yml tag job (pub.dev trusted publishing
  # only accepts OIDC from tag-push runs — a schedule/dispatch run can never
  # satisfy it). This leg VERIFIES pub.dev serves the pubspec version and,
  # when behind, recovers by re-running the failed tag-push publish run —
  # a rerun keeps the original push-tag event and OIDC claims, so the real
  # publish path retries. Unrecoverable states fail loudly and self-file an
  # issue with a manual-publish instruction instead of silently hanging.
  # gh-1192: a tag-publish still EXECUTING (tag pushed, ci run not visible
  # yet or queued/in_progress, tag younger than the grace window) is
  # classified «release in flight» by scripts/verify_pubdev_release.sh —
  # a neutral skip (no error, no auto-filed issue); the next scheduled
  # daily re-verifies. The 2026-10-03 collision fired the old «no ci.yml
  # run» error one minute before the healthy run completed (#1189, false
  # alarm). gh-1522: the version under test is the LATEST REMOTE TAG (the
  # committed pubspec is the 0.0.0-dev placeholder), so the «tag not cut
  # yet» state no longer exists.

  pubdev:
    name: 'Leg: pub.dev'
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 60
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: write # gh run rerun of the tag-publish run
    if: >-
      (needs.plan.outputs.changed == 'true' || inputs.force == true) &&
      (inputs.legs == '' || inputs.legs == 'all' || inputs.legs == 'pubdev')
    outputs:
      status: ${{ steps.check.outputs.status }}
      pubspec_version: ${{ steps.check.outputs.pubspec }}
      published_version: ${{ steps.check.outputs.published }}
      run_url: ${{ steps.check.outputs.run_url }}
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Inject failure (test)
        if: inputs.inject_failure == 'pubdev'
        run: |
          echo "::error::injected failure (inject_failure=pubdev) — exercising the self-filing issue path, nothing published"
          exit 1

      # gh-1561: the never-triggered self-heal re-pushes the latest tag with
      # the fa-release-bot App token — a GITHUB_TOKEN push can never cascade
      # (gh-1172), the App's push can (the same mechanism ci.yml's release
      # job uses to cut tags). Job-scoped, expires with the job; this job's
      # own GITHUB_TOKEN stays read-scoped (job-level permissions block).
      # Shape mirrors the validator-proven precedent (ci.yml release job,
      # the create-github-app-token step): NO `if:` at all — secrets
      # context in a step-if trips GitHub's workflow validator; and a mint
      # on an unconfigured App (forks, rotation gap) fails, is SWALLOWED by
      # continue-on-error, outputs.token stays empty, and the script's
      # manual-re-push alarm fires exactly as before this change.
      # Least privilege, verified against the PINNED action (v3.2.0,
      # bcd2ba49 — review thread 10): the composite `permissions` input
      # does NOT exist there (action.yml defines only the generated
      # `permission-*` inputs — GitHub warns `Unexpected input(s)
      # 'permissions'` and the action never reads it; ci.yml:3980 rides
      # that warning). The HONORED ceiling is the granular
      # `permission-contents` input, which the action turns into the mint
      # request's permissions map: contents:write only — the tag re-push —
      # instead of the installation's full grant set. Without it the token
      # inherits every permission the fa-release-bot installation has.
      - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@64ab729a6294000f5aa4a4bc0b73d1f32bc45510 # v3.3.0
        id: app-token
        continue-on-error: true
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          permission-contents: write

      - name: Verify pub.dev serves the pubspec version
        id: check
        # gh-1192: the classification (up-to-date / release-in-flight /
        # recovered + the unchanged alarms) lives in the extracted script so
        # it is shell-harness testable (test/release_flow_race_test.dart).
        # RELEASE_APP_TOKEN is empty when the mint above skipped (App not
        # configured) — the script then fails over to the manual-re-push
        # alarm instead of attempting a re-arm.
        env:
          RELEASE_APP_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}
        run: bash scripts/verify_pubdev_release.sh

  # ── Release-draft sweeper (issue #282) ────────────────────────────────────
  # Hygiene leg: no pipeline step may leave a draft release behind (the
  # 3-week-old v0.1.190 rot). The per-job guards in build-macos/build-mobile
  # own the failure path; this sweeper is the daily backstop — anything that
  # slips through (a cancelled run, a path without a guard) is deleted after
  # 24h and a deduplicated self-closing issue names the creating run so a
  # RECURRING stuck draft points at its broken step instead of rotting.
  # Exception (gh-236): the machine loop's artefact-cache drafts
  # (ai-gh-*/ai-pr-* — per-ticket session-snapshot storage) are
  # lifecycle-managed, not findings: reclaimed the moment their ticket
  # closes, swept after 24h while parked, kept while in flight — so the
  # sweep issue auto-closes when only cache traffic remains.
  # Runs on every daily (and manual) invocation regardless of leg results —
  # change-gating must not gate hygiene.
  sweep-drafts:
    name: Sweep stale release drafts
    needs: plan
    if: always() # even when plan failed or all legs skipped
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: write # delete draft releases
      actions: read # name each swept draft's creating run (gh run list 403s without it, review of #294)
      issues: write # deduplicated self-closing sweep issue
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
      # gh-2287: the machine-account identity — drafts authored by it are
      # pipeline-created (stale ones swept), not human (kept, E1). Same
      # env var + default as daily_publish_report.sh; the script works
      # without it, the export keeps the wiring reviewable.
      DAILY_PUBLISH_ASSIGNEE: ai-teammate
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Delete drafts older than 24h and file the dedup issue
        run: bash scripts/sweep_stale_drafts.sh

  # ── Report + self-healing issues ─────────────────────────────────────────
  report:
    name: Summary + self-filed issues
    needs: [plan, testflight, play, pubdev, cli, website, addin]
    if: always() # runs even when plan failed, so plan failures enter the self-healing loop too
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: read
      issues: write
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Job summary table and issue lifecycle
        env:
          NEXT_TAG: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.next_tag }}
          PLAN_RESULT: ${{ needs.plan.result }}
          DAILY_PUBLISH_ASSIGNEE: ai-teammate
          LEG_TESTFLIGHT: ${{ needs.testflight.result }}
          LEG_TESTFLIGHT_URL: ${{ needs.testflight.outputs.run_url }}
          LEG_PLAY: ${{ needs.play.result }}
          LEG_PLAY_URL: ${{ needs.play.outputs.run_url }}
          LEG_PUBDEV: ${{ needs.pubdev.result }}
          LEG_PUBDEV_STATUS: ${{ needs.pubdev.outputs.status }}
          LEG_PUBDEV_PUBSPEC: ${{ needs.pubdev.outputs.pubspec_version }}
          LEG_PUBDEV_PUBLISHED: ${{ needs.pubdev.outputs.published_version }}
          LEG_PUBDEV_URL: ${{ needs.pubdev.outputs.run_url }}
          LEG_CLI: ${{ needs.cli.result }}
          LEG_CLI_URL: ${{ needs.cli.outputs.run_url }}
          LEG_WEBSITE: ${{ needs.website.result }}
          LEG_WEBSITE_URL: ${{ needs.website.outputs.run_url }}
          LEG_ADDIN: ${{ needs.addin.result }}
          LEG_ADDIN_URL: ${{ needs.addin.outputs.run_url }}
        run: bash scripts/daily_publish_report.sh

      # gh-1478: the inject_failure TEST hook must prove the filed digest
      # QUOTES the injected ::error:: line (signal-first excerpt via the
      # per-job log endpoint), not merely that an issue exists — the #1473
      # tree-noise regression class.
      # The `!= ''` guard matters: on schedule triggers the `inputs` context
      # is EMPTY (the dispatch `default: none` does not apply), so gating
      # only on `!= 'none'` would run — and fail — this step every cron run.
      - name: Verify injected-failure excerpt (TEST)
        if: always() && inputs.inject_failure != '' && inputs.inject_failure != 'none'
        env:
          INJECTED: ${{ inputs.inject_failure }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          title="[daily-publish] ${INJECTED} leg failed"
          n=$(gh issue list --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --state open \
                --label daily-publish --limit 200 \
                --json number,title --jq '.[] | [.number, .title] | @tsv' \
                | while IFS=$'\t' read -r num t; do
                    [ "$t" = "$title" ] && echo "$num"
                  done | head -1)
          if [ -z "$n" ]; then
            echo "::error::inject_failure verify: no open issue titled '${title}' — the self-filing path regressed"
            exit 1
          fi
          text=$(gh issue view "$n" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" \
                   --json body,comments --jq '.body, (.comments[]?.body // empty)')
          if ! grep -qF "injected failure (inject_failure=${INJECTED})" <<< "$text"; then
            echo "::error::inject_failure verify: issue #${n} never quotes the injected ::error:: line — the signal-first excerpt regressed (gh-1478)"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "inject_failure verify OK: issue #${n} quotes the injected error line (gh-1478)"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Daily release-draft sweeper (issue #282), rides daily-publish.yml:
#
#   - lists DRAFT releases older than $SWEEP_MAX_AGE_SECONDS (default 24h);
#   - deletes stale drafts created by the pipeline (author.type == Bot, a
#     *[bot] login, the repo's machine account (DAILY_PUBLISH_ASSIGNEE,
#     default ai-teammate — gh-2287: its drafts (ai-gh-*/ai-pr-*) are
#     User-typed and marker-less but machine-created), OR the body
#     carries a well-formed `release-draft-owner: run/<id>/job/<job>`
#     marker — the exact shape
#     release_lazy_draft.sh / release_attach_or_create.sh stamp and
#     release_draft_guard.sh parses; since the drafts are created with
#     GH_TOKEN=RELEASE_PAT the API author is the PAT's human owner, so
#     the marker is the only ownership proof, gh-2008. Prose that merely
#     MENTIONS the substring or a malformed marker is NOT ownership —
#     those drafts stay human/kept, E1) — draft assets are unpublished by
#     definition and published releases are the artifact store, so
#     deletion is safe (issue #282 E2). The git tag is never touched;
#   - stale HUMAN drafts are listed in the summary, never deleted (E1);
#   - fresh drafts (<24h) are counted, never touched — an in-flight run
#     may legitimately own them. EXCEPTION (gh-2318): a fresh draft with a
#     well-formed release-draft-owner marker is RECLAIMED immediately when
#     its owner run completed, no ci.yml push train on the tag is still
#     queued/in-flight, and the tag's newest concluded ci.yml push train
#     failed with release-provenance SKIPPED (the publish point is
#     unreachable — rerun --failed cannot resurrect skipped jobs, so
#     nobody will ever publish it; the same criterion as ci.yml's gh-2230
#     train-draft-guard, which only sees drafts visible at train end).
#     A rerunnable (FAILED) provenance keeps the draft as the rerun
#     --failed recovery vessel (gh-1899) until it goes stale below;
#   - files ONE deduplicated, self-closing issue (label release-hygiene)
#     whenever anything stale was found — a comment on the open issue
#     instead of a duplicate, auto-closed again once a sweep comes up
#     clean (same convention as nightly.yml / daily_publish_report.sh).
#
# ── artefact-cache drafts have their own lifecycle (gh-236) ────────────────
# The machine loop (dmtools-agents factory: timerAutoCommitAndSave.js →
# releaseArtefacts.uploadRawFile → github_get_or_create_draft_release, tag
# template `ai-{ticketKey}`) writes every fa leg's session/output snapshots
# as assets of a per-ticket DRAFT release `ai-gh-<n>` / `ai-pr-<n>`, created
# with the ai-teammate token — User-typed, marker-less, no Actions run owns
# it. Those drafts are caches by design (never published, assets
# best-effort), NOT failed release-train drafts — but without a lifecycle
# they rotted 24h, were swept as generic bot-bucket findings, and re-filed
# the recurring sweep issue every day (gh-2287 → gh-2318 → gh-236). The
# guard: a machine-account draft whose tag matches `ai-(gh|pr)-<digits>` is
#   - RECLAIMED NOW, any age, when the ticket entity is `closed` — a closed
#     cycle never resumes (a reopened ticket starts a fresh session; the
#     pack's restore path is non-fatal and recreates the cache on "first
#     run"), so the draft is provably garbage the moment the cycle ends;
#   - swept by the existing 24h backstop when the ticket is still open (a
#     parked leg — the cache is recreated if the leg resumes);
#   - kept untouched while the ticket is open and the draft is fresh (an
#     in-flight leg may be writing snapshots into it);
#   - KEPT on any ticket-state lookup failure (never delete blind) — only
#     the 24h backstop then applies.
# The class is EXCLUDED from the sweep-issue finding counters: reclaiming a
# lifecycle-managed cache is routine hygiene, not a stale-draft finding, so
# the issue auto-closes when only cache traffic remains. Human-authored
# `ai-*` drafts are NOT lifecycle-managed (E1 holds — they stay listed,
# kept), and machine-authored non-matching drafts (e.g. a machine-authored
# `vX.Y.Z` train draft) stay in the bot bucket and remain findings.
#
# Drafts are deleted by release id via the API: a draft may carry an empty
# tag_name, which makes every tag-based `gh release delete` ambiguous.
#
# Env: GITHUB_REPOSITORY, GH_TOKEN, SWEEP_MAX_AGE_SECONDS (default 86400),
#      SWEEP_LABEL (default release-hygiene).
set -euo pipefail

repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:?GITHUB_REPOSITORY must be set}"
max_age="${SWEEP_MAX_AGE_SECONDS:-86400}"
label="${SWEEP_LABEL:-release-hygiene}"
# The repo's machine-account identity (same env + default as
# daily_publish_report.sh): drafts authored by it are pipeline-created —
# gh-2287: the ai-teammate factory's drafts (ai-gh-*/ai-pr-*) are User-typed
# and marker-less, so author-only Bot detection bucketed them as human and
# they rotted forever while the sweep issue never auto-closed.
assignee="${DAILY_PUBLISH_ASSIGNEE:-ai-teammate}"
title="[daily-publish] stale release drafts swept"
daily_url="${GITHUB_SERVER_URL:-https://github.com}/$repo/actions/runs/${GITHUB_RUN_ID:-manual}"

# ── failed-train diagnosis (gh-2105 + gh-2318) ──────────────────────────────
# The staged draft's publish owner is the TAG TRAIN (ci.yml's push run on
# the tag ref — release-provenance is the sole publish point, gh-1801).
# Diagnose <tag>'s newest CONCLUDED failed ci.yml push train; prints one
# TSV row:
#
#   train_id <TAB> conclusion <TAB> url <TAB> failed_jobs <TAB> prov_conclusion <TAB> in_flight
#
# `failed_jobs` names the train's failure-concluded jobs (the gh-2105 issue
# prose). `prov_conclusion` is the release-provenance job's OWN conclusion —
# "skipped" means the publish point is UNREACHABLE (`rerun --failed` never
# resurrects skipped jobs — the gh-2230 train-guard criterion), "failure"
# means it is rerunnable (the staged draft is the `rerun --failed` recovery
# vessel, gh-1899 — the stale 24h sweep reclaims it if the train is never
# recovered). `in_flight` is "in_flight" when ANY fetched ci.yml push run
# on the tag has a null conclusion (queued or in progress), "none" when all
# have concluded, and "unknown" if that check fails; the fresh-draft reclaim
# keeps unless it is explicitly "none", because a live train may still
# publish even when an older train failed. The publish-point job is matched
# by its ci.yml `name:` —
# "Sign release checksums" (pinned by test/release_stale_draft_reclaim_test.dart,
# gh-2318 group; update both together). Empty output = no failed train /
# lookup failed; every consumer degrades fail-safe (keep), and nothing
# here may gate the stale >24h delete (the diagnosis is never a
# precondition — gh-2105).
train_diagnosis() {
  local tag="$1" train_json failed_train train_id jobs_json in_flight
  train_json=$(gh run list --repo "$repo" --workflow ci.yml \
    --branch "$tag" --event push --limit 5 \
    --json databaseId,conclusion,url 2>/dev/null || echo "[]")
  in_flight=$(printf '%s' "$train_json" | jq -r '
    if any(.[]; .conclusion == null) then "in_flight" else "none" end
  ' 2>/dev/null || echo "unknown")
  failed_train=$(printf '%s' "$train_json" | jq -cr '
    ([.[] | select(.conclusion != "success" and .conclusion != null)][0]
      | if . == null then empty else
          {c: .conclusion, u: (.url // ""), i: .databaseId}
        end)' 2>/dev/null || echo "")
  [ -n "$failed_train" ] || return 0
  train_id=$(printf '%s' "$failed_train" | jq -r '.i // ""' 2>/dev/null || echo "")
  jobs_json=$(gh run view "$train_id" --repo "$repo" --json jobs 2>/dev/null || echo "")
  printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s' \
    "$train_id" \
    "$(printf '%s' "$failed_train" | jq -r '.c // "unknown"' 2>/dev/null || echo "unknown")" \
    "$(printf '%s' "$failed_train" | jq -r '.u // ""' 2>/dev/null || echo "")" \
    "$(printf '%s' "$jobs_json" | jq -r '[.jobs[] | select(.conclusion == "failure") | .name] | join(", ")' 2>/dev/null || echo "")" \
    "$(printf '%s' "$jobs_json" | jq -r '([.jobs[] | select(.name == "Sign release checksums")][0].conclusion // "")' 2>/dev/null || echo "")" \
    "$in_flight"
}


gh label create "$label" --repo "$repo" --color B60205 \
  --description "Auto-filed by the release-draft sweeper" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

# ── inventory ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# gh api --paginate emits one JSON array per page; the jq stream filter
# flattens them all. Bucketing happens in jq so the whole rule is
# reviewable in one place:
#   artifacts (machine account + ai-(gh|pr)-<n> tag — gh-236)
#                    -> lifecycle-managed: reclaim at cycle end / 24h
#                    backstop / keep in flight; NEVER a sweep finding
#   stale + pipeline (bot author, the machine account, or well-formed
#                    release-draft-owner: run/<id>/job/<job>
#                    marker in the body) -> delete, name the marker run
#   stale + human (no marker)          -> keep, list
#   fresh                              -> untouched, EXCEPT the gh-2318
#                    reclaim: a marked draft whose owner run completed and
#                    whose tag's train failed with release-provenance
#                    SKIPPED (publish point unreachable) is deleted NOW
drafts=$(gh api --paginate "repos/$repo/releases" | jq -r --argjson maxage "$max_age" --arg assignee "$assignee" '
  [ .[] | select(.draft == true)
    | { stale: ((now - (.created_at | fromdateiso8601)) > $maxage),
        bucket: (
          # gh-236 first: the machine loop artefact-cache class, keyed on
          # the machine account AND the `ai-{ticketKey}` tag shape the
          # factory releaseArtefacts.buildTag() produces (lowercased,
          # non-alnum to '-', so `GH-2288` becomes `ai-gh-2288`,
          # `pr-2293` becomes `ai-pr-2293`). Human-authored ai-* drafts and
          # machine-authored vX.Y.Z drafts never match and fall through to
          # the buckets below.
          if (((.author.login // "") == $assignee)
              and ((.tag_name // "") | test("^ai-(gh|pr)-[0-9]+$")))
          then "artifacts"
          elif ((now - (.created_at | fromdateiso8601)) > $maxage)
          then (if ((.author.type // "User") == "Bot"
                    or ((.author.login // "") | test("\\[bot\\]$"))
                    or ((.author.login // "") == $assignee)
                    or ((.body // "") | test("release-draft-owner: run/[0-9]+/job/")))
               then "bot" else "human" end)
          else "fresh" end),
        tag: (.tag_name // "(untagged)"),
        id: (.id | tostring),
        created: (.created_at // "?"),
        author: (.author.login // "unknown"),
        # Exact creating run parsed from the ownership marker ("" for
        # non-marker drafts) — the creating run executed on main, so a
        # tag-ref run lookup cannot find it (gh-2008). The array wrapper
        # keeps exactly one value: a bare capture(...)? on a non-matching
        # body yields an EMPTY stream, and an empty field would drop the
        # whole draft row from the object stream.
        run: ([ (.body // "")
                | capture("release-draft-owner: run/(?<run>[0-9]+)/")?
                | .run ]
              | .[0] // "") } ]
  | sort_by(.created)[]
  # Column order matters: `read` collapses runs of whitespace IFS chars, so
  # the only possibly-EMPTY field (.run — marker-less drafts) must stay
  # LAST; .stale sits before it (gh-236: the artifacts branch branches on it).
  | [ .bucket, .tag, .id, .created, .author, .stale, .run ] | @tsv')

deleted=""
deleted_tags=""
deleted_count=0
failed_trains=0
# gh-2318: fresh (<24h) pipeline drafts reclaimed early — provably
# never-publishable (completed owner, failed train with skipped
# release-provenance). Tracked separately from the >24h sweep deletions.
reclaimed=""
reclaimed_tags=""
reclaimed_count=0
humans=""
human_tags=""
fresh_count=0
# gh-236: machine-loop artefact-cache drafts — lifecycle-managed, NOT
# sweep findings (reclaiming a cache whose ticket cycle ended is routine
# hygiene; the issue must auto-close when only cache traffic remains).
#   reclaimed at cycle end (ticket closed, any age) / swept by the 24h
#   backstop (ticket still open / state unknown) / kept (fresh + open).
art_reclaimed=""
art_reclaimed_tags=""
art_reclaimed_count=0
art_swept=""
art_swept_tags=""
art_swept_count=0
art_kept_tags=""
art_kept_count=0

while IFS=$'\t' read -r bucket tag id created author stale marker_run; do
  [ -n "$bucket" ] || continue
  case "$bucket" in
    artifacts)
      # gh-236: the machine loop's per-ticket artefact-cache draft
      # (`ai-gh-<n>` / `ai-pr-<n>` — timerAutoCommitAndSave.js snapshot
      # storage). The tag shape was validated by the jq bucket rule, so
      # `gh #<num>` / `pr #<num>` parsing below is total. State lookup:
      # the issues REST API serves PRs too (state=closed covers merged).
      # Any lookup failure yields an empty state — fail-safe: no early
      # reclaim, only the 24h backstop below may delete.
      rest="${tag#ai-}"
      kind="${rest%%-*}"
      num="${rest##*-}"
      state=$(gh api "repos/$repo/issues/$num" 2>/dev/null \
        | jq -r '.state // ""' 2>/dev/null || echo "")
      if [ "$state" = "closed" ]; then
        gh api -X DELETE "repos/$repo/releases/$id" >/dev/null
        art_reclaimed_count=$((art_reclaimed_count + 1))
        art_reclaimed="$art_reclaimed- \`$tag\` — created $created by @$author; ticket cycle ended (\`$kind #$num\` closed) — reclaimed at cycle end, no 24h wait: a closed cycle never resumes and the cache is recreated on any future first run (gh-236)\n"
        art_reclaimed_tags="$art_reclaimed_tags $tag"
      elif [ "$stale" = "true" ]; then
        gh api -X DELETE "repos/$repo/releases/$id" >/dev/null
        art_swept_count=$((art_swept_count + 1))
        art_swept="$art_swept- \`$tag\` — created $created by @$author; swept after 24h with the ticket still open or its state unknown (parked leg — the cache is recreated if the leg resumes; gh-236)\n"
        art_swept_tags="$art_swept_tags $tag"
      else
        art_kept_count=$((art_kept_count + 1))
        art_kept_tags="$art_kept_tags $tag"
      fi
      ;;
    fresh)
      # gh-2318: "fresh — untouched" is right while an in-flight run may
      # own the draft, but a fresh draft can already be PROVABLY
      # never-publishable: the v1.0.739 shape — a daily-child staging leg
      # minted the tag (release_tag_mint.sh) and staged the draft, the
      # freshly fired train failed upstream of release-provenance, and the
      # gh-2230 train-draft-guard either ran before the draft existed (a
      # long attach leg created it later) or kept it while its owner was
      # still in-flight. Nothing re-examined such a draft with train
      # knowledge, so it rotted the full 24h and re-filed the recurring
      # sweep issue. Apply the train guard's EXACT criterion here —
      # reclaim only a well-formed-marker draft whose owner run COMPLETED,
      # whose tag has NO queued/in-flight ci.yml push train, and whose
      # newest concluded ci.yml push train failed with release-provenance
      # SKIPPED (rerun --failed cannot resurrect skipped jobs — nobody
      # will ever publish it). Fail-safe keeps mirror the train guard:
      # unmarked/human drafts (E1), an in-flight owner run (possibly
      # mid-upload), ANY queued/in-flight tag train (it may still publish
      # even when an older train failed), a rerunnable FAILED provenance
      # (that draft stays the `rerun --failed` recovery vessel, gh-1899,
      # until the stale sweep), any lookup failure (never delete blind),
      # and untagged drafts (no train to diagnose).
      if [ -n "$marker_run" ] && [ "$tag" != "(untagged)" ]; then
        owner_status=$(gh run view "$marker_run" --repo "$repo" --json status 2>/dev/null \
          | jq -r '.status // empty' 2>/dev/null || echo "")
        if [ "$owner_status" = "completed" ]; then
          diag=$(train_diagnosis "$tag")
          train_url_found=$(printf '%s' "$diag" | cut -f3)
          failed_jobs=$(printf '%s' "$diag" | cut -f4)
          prov_conclusion=$(printf '%s' "$diag" | cut -f5)
          train_conclusion=$(printf '%s' "$diag" | cut -f2)
          train_in_flight=$(printf '%s' "$diag" | cut -f6)
          if [ -n "$diag" ] && [ "$prov_conclusion" = "skipped" ] \
            && [ "$train_in_flight" = "none" ]; then
            gh api -X DELETE "repos/$repo/releases/$id" >/dev/null
            reclaimed_count=$((reclaimed_count + 1))
            failed_trains=$((failed_trains + 1))
            run_url="${GITHUB_SERVER_URL:-https://github.com}/$repo/actions/runs/$marker_run"
            train_line="  - tag train: ${train_url_found:-<url unavailable>} concluded ${train_conclusion:-unknown} — the staged draft was never published (release-provenance, the sole publish point, is gated behind the tag train; a superseded failed train is never rerun — verify_pubdev_release.sh heals the LATEST tag only)"
            [ -n "$failed_jobs" ] && train_line="$train_line; failed jobs: $failed_jobs"
            reclaimed="$reclaimed- \`$tag\` — created $created by @$author; creating run: $run_url\n  - reclaimed early: the draft is younger than $((max_age / 3600))h but its publish point is unreachable (failed train, skipped release-provenance — rerun --failed cannot resurrect skipped jobs), so no in-flight run can own it and nobody will ever publish it (gh-2318)\n$train_line\n"
            reclaimed_tags="$reclaimed_tags $tag"
            continue
          fi
        fi
      fi
      fresh_count=$((fresh_count + 1))
      ;;
    human)
      humans="$humans- \`$tag\` — created $created by @$author (human draft: listed, kept)\n"
      human_tags="$human_tags $tag"
      ;;
    bot)
      gh api -X DELETE "repos/$repo/releases/$id" >/dev/null
      deleted_count=$((deleted_count + 1))
      # Name the creating run so a RECURRING stuck draft points at its
      # broken step instead of rotting silently (AC2). Marker drafts name
      # it exactly (the stamping scripts write run/<id>); untagged
      # author-bot drafts fall back to the newest run on the tag ref;
      # dispatch-time drafts have no run on their ref — then say so.
      run_url=""
      if [ -n "$marker_run" ]; then
        run_url="${GITHUB_SERVER_URL:-https://github.com}/$repo/actions/runs/$marker_run"
      elif [ "$tag" != "(untagged)" ]; then
        run_url=$(gh run list --repo "$repo" --branch "$tag" --limit 1 \
          --json url --jq '.[0].url // empty' 2>/dev/null || true)
      fi
      if [ -z "$run_url" ]; then
        if [ "$author" = "$assignee" ]; then
          # gh-2287: a machine-account draft carries no marker (the
          # automation created it with its own token, outside this repo's
          # runners) — name the account as the creator; the dispatch-time
          # "creating step died mid-run" prose below would misdirect the
          # RCA (gh-2105 class) — nothing died.
          run_url="the @$assignee automation loop (machine-account draft — created outside this repo's runners, no Actions run owns it)"
        else
          run_url="no run on ref \`$tag\` (dispatch-time draft — the creating step died mid-run)"
        fi
      fi
      # gh-2105: the staging draft's publish owner is the TAG TRAIN
      # (ci.yml's push run on the tag ref — release-provenance is the
      # sole publish point, gh-1801). When that train failed, the
      # creating run named above is NOT the broken step — the train is,
      # and a superseded failed train is never rerun
      # (verify_pubdev_release.sh heals the LATEST tag only). Name it
      # (URL + conclusion + failed jobs) so the sweep issue points at
      # the true blocker. Any lookup failure degrades to the static
      # prose below — the delete + issue filing must never depend on
      # the diagnosis.
      train_line=""
      if [ "$tag" != "(untagged)" ]; then
        diag=$(train_diagnosis "$tag")
        if [ -n "$diag" ]; then
          train_conclusion=$(printf '%s' "$diag" | cut -f2)
          train_url_found=$(printf '%s' "$diag" | cut -f3)
          failed_jobs=$(printf '%s' "$diag" | cut -f4)
          failed_trains=$((failed_trains + 1))
          train_line="  - tag train: ${train_url_found:-<url unavailable>} concluded ${train_conclusion:-unknown} — the staged draft was never published (release-provenance, the sole publish point, is gated behind the tag train; a superseded failed train is never rerun — verify_pubdev_release.sh heals the LATEST tag only)"
          [ -n "$failed_jobs" ] && train_line="$train_line; failed jobs: $failed_jobs"
          train_line="$train_line\n"
        fi
      fi
      deleted="$deleted- \`$tag\` — created $created by @$author; creating run: $run_url\n$train_line"
      deleted_tags="$deleted_tags $tag"
      ;;
  esac
done <<< "$drafts"

# ── issue lifecycle (dedup + self-closing) ─────────────────────────────────
find_open_issue() { # echoes the issue number of the open sweep issue, or nothing
  gh issue list --repo "$repo" --state open --label "$label" \
    --limit 100 --json number,title --jq '.[] | [.number, .title] | @tsv' 2>/dev/null \
    | while IFS=$'\t' read -r n t; do
        if [ "$t" = "$title" ]; then echo "$n"; fi
      done | head -1
}

same_run_issues() { # gh-2359 AC3: open issues already filed from THIS run
  # The run URL is the join key (the leg-filer embeds the same
  # **Daily run:**/**Sweep run:** URL): a sweep finding and a leg failure
  # from one daily run (the #2336/#2337 shape) share roots even though
  # their error signatures never match.
  # gh itself has no --arg flag — the filter runs through real jq, exactly
  # like this script's `gh api --paginate … | jq -r --arg …` draft lookups.
  gh issue list --repo "$repo" --state open --limit 200 --json number,body \
    2>/dev/null \
    | jq -r --arg run_url "$daily_url" \
      '.[] | select((.body // "") | contains($run_url)) | .number' \
    || true
}

stale_count=$((deleted_count + reclaimed_count + $(printf '%s' "$humans" | grep -c . || true) ))

if [ "$stale_count" -gt 0 ]; then
  body=$(mktemp)
  {
    echo "**Sweep run:** $daily_url"
    echo "**Swept:** $deleted_count stale pipeline-created draft(s) older than $((max_age / 3600))h"
    printf '%b' "$deleted"
    # gh-2318: fresh drafts reclaimed early — their publish point is
    # unreachable, so the 24h wait would only delay the inevitable and
    # keep the sweep issue recurring (see the branch comment for the
    # full fail-safe keep list).
    if [ "$reclaimed_count" -gt 0 ]; then
      echo
      echo "**Reclaimed early (<$((max_age / 3600))h):** $reclaimed_count fresh pipeline draft(s) whose publish point is unreachable (gh-2318)"
      printf '%b' "$reclaimed"
    fi
    [ -n "$humans" ] && { echo; echo "**Kept (human drafts, listed not deleted — E1):**"; printf '%b' "$humans"; }
    # gh-236: cache lifecycle activity rides the filed issue for
    # visibility — in its own section, with the release-failure prose
    # never attached (nothing died, nothing failed to publish). It does
    # NOT contribute to the finding count above.
    if [ "$((art_reclaimed_count + art_swept_count))" -gt 0 ]; then
      echo
      echo "**Artefact-cache drafts (machine-loop \`ai-gh-*\`/\`ai-pr-*\` caches — lifecycle-managed, not release failures):** $art_reclaimed_count reclaimed at cycle end, $art_swept_count swept after 24h"
      printf '%b' "$art_reclaimed"
      printf '%b' "$art_swept"
    fi
    echo
    echo "**Fresh drafts (<$((max_age / 3600))h):** $fresh_count — untouched (an in-flight run may own them)"
    if [ "$art_kept_count" -gt 0 ]; then
      echo "**Artefact-cache drafts kept (ticket in flight):** $art_kept_count — reclaimed when the cycle closes, swept after 24h if parked (gh-236)"
    fi
    echo
    if [ "$failed_trains" -gt 0 ]; then
      echo "**Failed tag trains named above:** $failed_trains"
      echo
      echo "A stale draft whose tag train failed means the publish owner never ran — the draft was the gh-1801 staging draft and release-provenance (its sole publish point) is gated behind the failed train. Rerun the train if the tag should still ship; recurrence means a lifecycle guard is missing (issue #282)."
    elif [ "$deleted_count" -gt 0 ]; then
      echo "A stale draft means a \`gh release create\` step died between asset upload and publish — check the creating run's failed step. Recurrence means a lifecycle guard is missing (issue #282)."
    else
      # Findings are kept human drafts only (gh-236: cache lifecycle
      # traffic is excluded from the finding counters) — the create-death
      # prose would misdirect: nothing died and nothing failed to publish.
      echo "Kept human drafts above are listed, never deleted (E1) — delete by hand once done with them. Machine-loop artefact-cache drafts (\`ai-gh-*\`/\`ai-pr-*\`) are lifecycle-managed (gh-236): reclaimed when their ticket cycle closes, swept after 24h when the ticket stays open or its state is unknown."
    fi
    echo
    echo "---"
    echo "Auto-filed by the daily draft sweeper; auto-closes when a sweep finds nothing stale."
  } > "$body"
  existing=$(find_open_issue)
  # gh-2359 AC3: peers computed BEFORE the create (eventual consistency).
  peers=$(same_run_issues)
  if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
    gh issue comment "$existing" --repo "$repo" --body-file "$body" >/dev/null
    issue_action="commented on #$existing (still finding stale drafts)"
  else
    created_issue=$(gh issue create --repo "$repo" --title "$title" \
      --body-file "$body" --label bug --label "$label" --assignee "$assignee" 2>/dev/null || true)
    issue_action="filed ${created_issue:-<issue creation failed>}"
    if [ -n "$created_issue" ] && [ -n "$peers" ]; then
      # gh-2359 AC3: the sweep finding is filed from the same run as
      # another open issue (typically a leg failure) — cross-link so the
      # shared root is visible before anyone fixes each in parallel.
      peer_list=$(printf '%s' "$peers" | awk '{printf "%s#%s", (NR > 1 ? ", " : ""), $1}')
      gh issue comment "${created_issue##*/}" --repo "$repo" \
        --body "**Same-run cross-link (gh-2359):** same run as ${peer_list} — roots may be shared. One failing run can surface as several findings; check whether a single root cause covers them before fixing each in parallel." >/dev/null
      issue_action+=" + cross-linked with same-run issue(s) ${peer_list}"
    fi
  fi
  rm -f "$body"
else
  existing=$(find_open_issue)
  issue_action="none needed"
  if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
    gh issue close "$existing" --repo "$repo" \
      --comment "✅ sweep found nothing stale — auto-closing." >/dev/null
    issue_action="auto-closed #$existing (clean sweep)"
  fi
fi

# ── job summary ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
{
  echo "### Release-draft sweeper"
  echo
  echo "Deleted **$deleted_count** stale pipeline-created draft(s) • reclaimed early: **$reclaimed_count** • artefact-cache (gh-236): **$art_reclaimed_count** reclaimed at cycle end, **$art_swept_count** swept, **$art_kept_count** kept • failed tag trains named: **$failed_trains** • kept human drafts: **$(printf '%s' "$humans" | grep -c . || true)** • fresh (<$((max_age / 3600))h): **$fresh_count** • issue lifecycle: $issue_action"
} >> "${GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY:-/dev/stdout}"

echo "sweeper: deleted=${deleted_tags# } reclaimed-early=${reclaimed_tags# } human-kept=${human_tags# } fresh=$fresh_count art-reclaimed=${art_reclaimed_tags# } art-swept=${art_swept_tags# } art-kept=$art_kept_count issue=$issue_action"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Attach assets to <tag>'s release, creating it when missing — the single
# draft-capable create path for build-macos.yml / build-mobile.yml
# (issue #282 E3 + review of #294).
#
# Race-idempotent (E3): if `gh release create` loses the view→create race
# (another job/run created the release in between), fall back to
# uploading into the winner's release instead of failing. A failed create
# would fire the job's draft lifecycle guard against the WINNER's
# in-flight draft.
#
# Ownership-stamped: the create path makes a DRAFT (gh-1801 rework: the
# release never goes live from a leg — the tag-run release-provenance job
# publishes + flags latest once the signed SHA256SUMS is attached). The
# body stamps
#   <!-- release-draft-owner: run/<run_id>/job/<job_id> -->
# and release_draft_guard.sh deletes that draft ONLY on an exact
# run+job match — never the sibling leg's mid-upload draft (daily-publish
# runs the mobile and macOS legs concurrently on the same derived tag).
# The marker is an invisible HTML comment in the body.
#
# Usage: release_attach_or_create.sh <tag> <asset> [<asset>...]
#   reads the release body from release-notes.md in the CWD (a minimal
#   body is written when the file is missing/empty)
# Env: GITHUB_REPOSITORY, GITHUB_RUN_ID, GITHUB_JOB (Actions defaults),
#      GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN.
set -euo pipefail

tag="${1:?usage: release_attach_or_create.sh <tag> <assets...>}"
repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:?GITHUB_REPOSITORY must be set}"
shift
assets=("$@")
if [ "${#assets[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
  # gh-1801 hard refusal: creating a release with zero resolved assets is
  # the `fa update` breaker (an empty `latest` 404s every
  # fa-<os>-<arch>.tar.gz until backfill — v1.0.630, 2026-10-23). Attaching
  # is the caller's only honest option when it resolved nothing — fail
  # loud here, never create empty. Pinned by
  # test/release_empty_latest_guard_test.dart.
  echo "::error::no assets to attach for $tag — refusing to create or touch a release with an empty asset list (gh-1801): resolve at least one artifact or skip the release step" >&2
  exit 1
fi

upload_all() { # exists-path: gate-guarded attach + (servable DRAFT-only) publish + latest
  # gh-2042 (AC1): every upload passes the immutability gate — on a
  # PUBLISHED release an unattached fa-* asset refuses the whole call loud,
  # an already-attached one skips, and non-fa store/DMG refreshers keep
  # their clobber-refresh contract. Drafts attach exactly as before.
  # gh-2042 (review): ONE call for the WHOLE list — the gate's contract is
  # per-call all-or-nothing ("refuse before any upload"), so per-asset
  # invocation would judge each asset against its own release-view
  # snapshot (N round-trips, a wider draft→published TOCTOU window, and a
  # partial mutation when an early benign asset uploads before a later
  # fa-* refusal).
  bash "$(dirname "$0")/release_asset_gate.sh" "$tag" "${assets[@]}"

  # when the release can actually serve `fa update` — that means the signed
  # checksums are already on it (`fa update` hard-fails without
  # SHA256SUMS(.sig), bin/self_manage.dart provenance gate) — AND it is
  # still a DRAFT (the provenance-flip recovery window). A PUBLISHED
  # release is never re-flaged `--latest` here: on an older release that
  # would drag the latest badge (and `fa update`) backwards to a downgrade.
  if release_serves_fa_update; then
    case "$(gh release view "$tag" --repo "$repo" --json isDraft --jq .isDraft 2>/dev/null || echo false)" in
      true)
        gh release edit "$tag" --draft=false --latest --repo "$repo"

        # minted by a sibling leg of THIS run would otherwise rot until the
        # 24h sweeper. The tag is published and servable here (the flip is
        # gated on the signed checksums), so own-run twin drafts are orphans.

          || echo "::warning::gh-1899 twin-draft dedupe failed — the release is published and servable, so this is cleanup noise only; the 24h sweeper remains the backstop"
        ;;
      *)
        echo "release $tag is already published — publish/latest flip skipped (gh-2042: latest never moves backwards; the signed SHA256SUMS re-upload is release-provenance's job)"
        ;;
    esac

    echo "release $tag is not yet servable (no SHA256SUMS on it) — publish+latest left to the release-provenance step (gh-1801)"
  fi

# fa-update servability = the signed checksums are on the release. Every
# fa-* archive alone is NOT enough: `fa update` fetches SHA256SUMS(.sig)
# and aborts when either is missing (bin/self_manage.dart).
release_serves_fa_update() {
  local names
  names=$(gh release view "$tag" --repo "$repo" --json assets --jq '.assets[].name' 2>/dev/null || true)
  printf '%s\n' "$names" | grep -qE '^SHA256SUMS(\.sig)?$'
}

if gh release view "$tag" --repo "$repo" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  upload_all
  echo "✅ attached ${#assets[@]} asset(s) to existing release $tag"
  exit 0
fi

# Body: prepared notes (CHANGELOG section / conventional-commit fallback)
# plus the ownership marker the guard verifies before deleting.
notes="release-notes.md"
[ -s "$notes" ] || printf 'Release %s — see the CHANGELOG.\n' "$tag" > "$notes"
bash "$(dirname "$0")/release_notes_cap.sh" "$notes"

# truncates from the TAIL, so a pre-stamped marker is cut off and the
# created draft carries no ownership proof: release_draft_guard.sh
# resolves `<unmarked>` and refuses to reclaim it, the daily sweeper
# buckets it human (the legs run with GH_TOKEN=RELEASE_PAT) and keeps
# it, dedupe ignores it — a forever-orphaned draft (gh-282). Bounded
# body (≤ 120,000) + the marker stays under GitHub's 125,000-character
# release-body cap whose overshoot HTTP-422'd the create in run
# 44680647719 (v1.0.756).
marker="<!-- release-draft-owner: run/${GITHUB_RUN_ID:?GITHUB_RUN_ID must be set (GitHub Actions default env)}/job/${GITHUB_JOB:?GITHUB_JOB must be set (GitHub Actions default env)} -->"
grep -qF "$marker" "$notes" || printf '\n%s\n' "$marker" >> "$notes"

# A `gh release create` for a MISSING tag mints a lightweight API tag:
# no push event → no ci.yml tag run → no publish/binaries (the v0.1.408
# silent class, issue #597). If the ref is absent, mint it as an
# ANNOTATED tag and push it with the PAT the job already carries
# (GH_TOKEN=RELEASE_PAT in build-macos) so the tag CI fires. The mint
# itself (GH_TOKEN guard, persisted-checkout-extraheader strip, push,
# train-start verification) lives in scripts/release_tag_mint.sh —
# gh-2026: the v1.0.663 / v1.0.665 minted pushes rode actions/checkout's
# persisted GITHUB_TOKEN extraheader (it outranks the URL credentials),
# GitHub suppresses workflow triggers for GITHUB_TOKEN pushes, no tag run
# ever existed on those refs, and the drafts rotted behind green legs.
# A mint whose train does not start now fails loud BEFORE any draft is
# created, so the leg goes red and the failure-path draft guard has
# nothing to reclaim.
# Gate on the DEFINITE missing verdict (ls-remote --exit-code rc 2):
# sandboxes without an origin remote fatal with 128 — indeterminable
# falls through to the plain create path (test fixtures rely on it).
set +e
git ls-remote --exit-code origin "refs/tags/$tag" >/dev/null 2>&1
ls_remote_rc=$?
set -e
if [ "$ls_remote_rc" -eq 2 ]; then
  bash "$(dirname "$0")/release_tag_mint.sh" "$tag"
fi

# Bare vX.Y.Z title (#282): matches the tag, matches pub.dev. gh-1801
# rework: the create is DRAFT-ONLY. Whatever this leg resolved
# (AAB/IPA/store APKs, DMGs/zips) is not the signed provenance `fa update`
# demands — a leg that arrives first must never publish the release, let
# alone flag it latest (threads 2/6). The draft is ownership-stamped (the
# marker below) so this job's draft lifecycle guard reclaims it on
# failure; the tag-run binaries job attaches the CLI assets into it and
# release-provenance (ci.yml) publishes + flags latest once SHA256SUMS.sig
# is on board.
if gh release create "$tag" \
  --repo "$repo" \
  --title "$tag" \
  --draft \
  --notes-file "$notes" \
  "${assets[@]}"; then
  echo "✅ created draft release $tag with ${#assets[@]} asset(s) — publish is provenance-owned (gh-1801)"
  exit 0
fi

# E3 idempotency: the create may have lost the view→create race — the
# winner's release now exists. Attach instead of failing (a failing
# create would fire the guard against the winner's in-flight draft).
if gh release view "$tag" --repo "$repo" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  upload_all
  echo "✅ lost the create race — attached ${#assets[@]} asset(s) to the concurrently created release $tag"
  exit 0
fi

echo "::error::release create for $tag failed and no concurrent release appeared — see the step log above" >&2
exit 1

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Release draft lifecycle guard (issue #282): a run that creates a release
# draft must end with it published or deleted — never orphan it. `gh
# release create <tag> <assets...>` uploads the assets through a DRAFT
# first and publishes only after every upload succeeds; a step dying
# mid-upload (the v0.1.190 rot) leaves that draft behind forever.
#
# Usage: release_draft_guard.sh <tag>
#
# OWNERSHIP-SCOPED DELETE (review of #294): the guard deletes ONLY the
# draft this very run+job created. daily-publish runs the macOS and
# mobile legs concurrently against the same derived tag; a failed leg's
# guard firing on the SIBLING leg's mid-upload draft would destroy a
# healthy concurrent release. Draft-capable creates
# (scripts/release_attach_or_create.sh, scripts/release_lazy_draft.sh)
# stamp the draft body with
#   <!-- release-draft-owner: run/<run_id>/job/<job_id> -->
# and the guard deletes only on an exact match against GITHUB_RUN_ID /
# GITHUB_JOB (both GitHub Actions default env). Matrix jobs share
# GITHUB_JOB across legs (ci.yml binaries, build-macos.yml
# build-macos-cli) — those steps stamp a LEG-SUFFIXED identity via
# RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY (e.g. run/123/job/binaries-linux-x64) and the
# guard step must export the same value, so a failed leg can never match
# a sibling's in-flight draft. A foreign or unmarked draft is NEVER
# deleted here — the daily sweeper
# (scripts/sweep_stale_drafts.sh) reclaims genuinely orphaned drafts
# after 24h.
#
# Called from workflow steps with `if: always() && job.status != 'success'`
# so it runs on failure AND cancellation. A published release or a missing
# release is a no-op; a draft for <tag> is deleted (its assets are
# unpublished by definition — published releases are the artifact store,
# issue #282 E2). The tag itself is never touched.
set -euo pipefail

tag="${1:?usage: release_draft_guard.sh <tag>}"
repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:?GITHUB_REPOSITORY must be set}"
: "${GITHUB_RUN_ID:?GITHUB_RUN_ID must be set (GitHub Actions default env)}"
: "${GITHUB_JOB:?GITHUB_JOB must be set (GitHub Actions default env)}"
identity="${RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY:-run/$GITHUB_RUN_ID/job/$GITHUB_JOB}"
# Validate (mirror of release_lazy_draft.sh): an unmatchable identity
# would silently orphan the draft forever.
printf '%s' "$identity" | grep -Eq '^run/[0-9]+/job/[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$' || {
  echo "::error::RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY '$identity' does not match 'run/<id>/job/<name>' — the marker could never be stamped or matched" >&2
  exit 1
}

state=$(gh release view "$tag" --repo "$repo" --json isDraft --jq .isDraft 2>/dev/null || echo missing)
if [ "$state" != "true" ]; then
  echo "release lifecycle guard: $tag is ${state} (published or absent) — nothing to clean"
  exit 0
fi

notes=$(gh release view "$tag" --repo "$repo" --json body --jq '.body // ""' 2>/dev/null || echo "")
owner=$(printf '%s' "$notes" \
  | grep -oE 'release-draft-owner: run/[0-9]+/job/[A-Za-z0-9_-]+' \
  | head -1 | sed 's/^release-draft-owner: //' || true)

if [ "$owner" != "$identity" ]; then
  echo "::warning::release lifecycle guard: draft $tag is owned by '${owner:-<unmarked>}' (we are $identity) — refusing to delete a draft this run+job did not create; a sibling leg may be mid-upload. The daily sweeper reclaims orphaned drafts after 24h (issue #282)."
  exit 0
fi

gh release delete "$tag" --repo "$repo" --yes
echo "::warning::release lifecycle guard: deleted own draft $tag — the run failed after creating it; a draft must be published or deleted, never orphaned (issue #282)"
