#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Post-publish orphan-draft twin cleanup (gh-1899).
#
# Why this exists: GitHub does NOT atomically enforce one release per tag.
# The lazy draft create (scripts/release_lazy_draft.sh) tolerates the
# view→create race with `|| true` on the assumption that a second
# `gh release create` for the same tag is rejected — it is not always:
# run 40163369302 (v1.0.641, fully green) created TWO draft releases for
# the same tag 87 ms apart (both binaries legs logged "lazy draft ready";
# duplicate-tag precedent: v0.1.120, release ids 363745676/363745677).
# release-provenance flips exactly ONE object to --draft=false --latest;
# the twin stays a draft forever — no failure-path guard can fire because
# every creating leg SUCCEEDED — so the only reclaimer was the 24h
# sweeper, which deleted the twin and filed the recurring
# "[daily-publish] stale release drafts swept" issue (gh-1899).
#
# This is the missing success-path half of the issue #282 invariant ("a
# run ends with its draft published or deleted — never orphaned") — the
# failure half lives in scripts/release_draft_guard.sh. Call it AFTER the
# publish flip (ci.yml release-provenance's "Upload provenance assets",
# release_attach_or_create.sh's servable-recovery publish):
#
#   - PRECONDITION: the tag must have a PUBLISHED release. A red
#     provenance (gh-1832 gate, signing) leaves the draft on purpose — it
#     is the recovery vessel for `gh run rerun --failed` — and this guard
#     must never take it away. No published release → no-op.
#   - Deletes every DRAFT for <tag> stamped with THIS run's ownership
#     marker (<!-- release-draft-owner: run/<GITHUB_RUN_ID>/job/<name> -->)
#     by release id via the API — those are proven orphan twins of the
#     just-published release, carrying unpublished-only assets (issue
#     #282 E2). The tag-based `gh release delete` is never used: under
#     duplicate releases a tag lookup is ambiguous, the very class this
#     guard exists for.
#   - Foreign-run and unmarked drafts are NEVER deleted here — the same
#     ownership discipline as release_draft_guard.sh; the daily sweeper
#     (scripts/sweep_stale_drafts.sh) reclaims those after 24h.
#
# Failure mode (gh-1899 review): every call site runs this script
# BEST-EFFORT (`|| echo "::warning::…"`) — it fires AFTER the publish
# flip, when the release is already published and servable, so a cleanup
# blip (rate limit, one failed DELETE) must never red the leg/job; the
# warning keeps it visible and the 24h sweeper remains the backstop.
#
# Usage: release_draft_dedupe.sh <tag>
# Env: GITHUB_REPOSITORY, GITHUB_RUN_ID (Actions defaults), GH_TOKEN/
#      GITHUB_TOKEN.
set -euo pipefail

tag="${1:?usage: release_draft_dedupe.sh <tag>}"
repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:?GITHUB_REPOSITORY must be set}"
: "${GITHUB_RUN_ID:?GITHUB_RUN_ID must be set (GitHub Actions default env)}"

# One listing, two questions. `gh api --paginate` concatenates one JSON
# array per page; -s flattens them into a single release roster before
# the filter runs (a per-page filter could miss a twin on another page).
list=$(gh api --paginate "repos/$repo/releases")

# PRECONDITION: the tag's release is published. Until the flip happens,
# a leftover draft is the recovery vessel, not an orphan.
if ! printf '%s' "$list" | jq -s -e --arg tag "$tag" \
    'flatten | any(.[]; .tag_name == $tag and .draft == false)' \
    >/dev/null; then
  echo "release draft dedupe: no published release for $tag — a leftover draft is the rerun --failed recovery vessel; nothing reclaimed (gh-1899)"
  exit 0
fi

# The marker's run segment is matched with its trailing slash so run/111
# can never match run/1111 (the prefix trap release_draft_guard.sh pins).
twins=$(printf '%s' "$list" | jq -s -r --arg tag "$tag" --arg run "run/$GITHUB_RUN_ID/" '
  [ flatten
    | .[]
    | select(.draft == true and .tag_name == $tag
        and ((.body // "") | contains("release-draft-owner: " + $run)))
    | .id | tostring ]
  | join("\n")')

if [ -z "$twins" ]; then
  echo "release draft dedupe: nothing to reclaim for $tag (no own-run twin drafts)"
  exit 0
fi

deleted=0
while IFS= read -r id; do
  [ -n "$id" ] || continue
  gh api -X DELETE "repos/$repo/releases/$id" >/dev/null
  deleted=$((deleted + 1))
  echo "::warning::release draft dedupe: deleted orphaned twin draft $id for $tag — the lazy-create race minted two releases for one tag and only one could be published (gh-1899); its assets were unpublished-only, the published release is the artifact store (issue #282 E2)"
done <<< "$twins"

echo "release draft dedupe: reclaimed $deleted orphaned twin draft(s) for $tag (gh-1899)"
=====LAZY=====
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Lazy DRAFT create for the release train's asset-upload steps (gh-1801).
#
# The train workflows (ci.yml binaries/web-spa, build-macos.yml
# build-macos-cli/build-extension) need a release object to attach assets
# to, but the release must never go live from an upload step: `fa update`
# resolves the `latest` release and hard-fails without the SIGNED
# SHA256SUMS(.sig) (bin/self_manage.dart provenance gate), which only the
# tag-run release-provenance job can upload. This script creates the
# release as a DRAFT — nothing else:
#
#   - body = scripts/release_notes.sh output (curated `## <version>`
#     CHANGELOG section → curated `## Unreleased` → conventional commits;
#     the gh-1172 curated-notes contract), with a minimal fallback —
#     never `--generate-notes` (review threads 3/7);
#   - body carries `<!-- release-draft-owner: run/<run_id>/job/<job> -->`
#     so scripts/release_draft_guard.sh can reclaim the draft on failure
#     (review threads 4/8) — matrix legs override the identity via
#     RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY (e.g. binaries-linux-x64) so a failed leg's
#     guard can never match a sibling's in-flight draft;
#   - the view→create race is tolerated (`|| true`): a sibling leg or the
#     attach path may create the release between our view and create —
#     the loser just uploads into the winner's release;
#   - it NEVER publishes and NEVER flags latest: the single publish point
#     of a tag train is release-provenance's "Upload provenance assets"
#     step (`gh release edit --draft=false --latest` after SHA256SUMS.sig
#     lands). A red provenance leaves the previous release as latest —
#     safe degradation, never a provenance-less latest (v1.0.630 window).
#
# Usage: release_lazy_draft.sh <tag>
# Env: GITHUB_REPOSITORY, GITHUB_RUN_ID, GITHUB_JOB (Actions defaults),
#      RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY (optional leg-suffixed override),
#      GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN.
set -euo pipefail

tag="${1:?usage: release_lazy_draft.sh <tag>}"
repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:?GITHUB_REPOSITORY must be set}"
identity="${RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY:-run/${GITHUB_RUN_ID:?GITHUB_RUN_ID must be set (GitHub Actions default env)}/job/${GITHUB_JOB:?GITHUB_JOB must be set (GitHub Actions default env)}}"

# The guard greps exactly this class — validate here so a malformed
# override fails loud instead of stamping a marker the guard could never
# match (a forever-orphaned draft).
printf '%s' "$identity" | grep -Eq '^run/[0-9]+/job/[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$' || {
  echo "::error::RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY '$identity' does not match 'run/<id>/job/<name>' — the draft lifecycle guard could never reclaim such a draft" >&2
  exit 1
}

# Already created (by a sibling leg, the attach path, or a previous run)?
# Drafts and published releases both resolve here — upload-only is safe.
if gh release view "$tag" --repo "$repo" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "release $tag already exists — lazy draft create skipped"
  exit 0
fi

# Body: curated notes (CHANGELOG section / Unreleased / conventional
# commits) plus the ownership marker the guard verifies before deleting.
# stderr is NOT swallowed: release_notes.sh's ::error gates (e.g. the
# duplicate-'## Unreleased' curation guard) must stay visible even when
# the minimal fallback below keeps the train moving.
notes_file="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/release-lazy-notes.XXXXXX")"
trap 'rm -f "$notes_file"' EXIT
if ! bash "$(dirname "$0")/release_notes.sh" "$tag" >"$notes_file" ||
  [ ! -s "$notes_file" ]; then
  printf 'Release %s — see the CHANGELOG.\n' "$tag" >"$notes_file"
fi
# gh-237: bound the body BEFORE stamping the owner marker — the cap
# truncates from the TAIL, so a pre-stamped marker is cut off and the
# created draft carries no ownership proof: release_draft_guard.sh
# resolves `<unmarked>` and refuses to reclaim it, the daily sweeper
# buckets it human (the legs run with GH_TOKEN=RELEASE_PAT) and keeps
# it, dedupe ignores it — a forever-orphaned draft (gh-282). Bounded
# body (≤ 120,000) + the marker stays under the 125,000-character
# release-body cap whose overshoot HTTP-422'd `gh release create` in
# run 44680647719 (v1.0.756) and left every attach gate on the tag
# dying with "release not found".
bash "$(dirname "$0")/release_notes_cap.sh" "$notes_file"

marker="<!-- release-draft-owner: $identity -->"
grep -qF "$marker" "$notes_file" || printf '\n%s\n' "$marker" >>"$notes_file"

# gh-2026: a `gh release create` for a MISSING ref REST-mints a
# lightweight API tag with NO push event — the v0.1.408 silent class
# (issue #597). The fast legs (build-macos.yml build-extension /
# build-macos-cli) can reach this create before the attach legs
# (release-macos / release-mobile): the silent mint wins the race, every
# attach leg then finds the tag existing and skips the CI-firing
# annotated push, no tag train ever runs, and the draft is stranded
# (swept a day later — the v1.0.663 / v1.0.665 shape). When the ref is
# DEFINITELY missing, mint it through the CI-firing annotated push and
# verify the train started BEFORE creating the draft (dispatch-time call
# sites export GH_TOKEN=RELEASE_PAT for exactly this; the ci.yml tag-run
# call sites always see the tag of their own push event and never enter
# the mint). An indeterminable verdict (no origin remote, rc 128 —
# sandboxed fixtures) falls through to the plain create path.
set +e
git ls-remote --exit-code origin "refs/tags/$tag" >/dev/null 2>&1
ls_remote_rc=$?
set -e
if [ "$ls_remote_rc" -eq 2 ]; then
  bash "$(dirname "$0")/release_tag_mint.sh" "$tag"
fi

# DRAFT-first (gh-1801): a create here must never publish — the resolved
# asset list at this point can never include the signed checksums. The
# race-lost create is tolerated (the winner owns the release), but a REAL
# create failure is not (gh-237): the body was already bounded above by
# release_notes_cap.sh, so a surviving failure is a genuine API error.
create_rc=0
gh release create "$tag" \
  --repo "$repo" \
  --title "$tag" \
  --draft \
  --notes-file "$notes_file" || create_rc=$?
if [ "$create_rc" -ne 0 ]; then
  # gh-1801's `|| true` tolerated ONLY the view→create race — a sibling
  # leg creating the release between our view and create. gh-237 (run
  # 44680647719, v1.0.756): that swallow ALSO ate real create failures
  # (body-too-long 422), printed "✅ lazy draft ready", and failed every
  # attach gate with "release not found". Re-view: the release existing
  # NOW means we lost the race (upload into the winner's release); it
  # still being missing means the create itself failed — the leg must
  # go red, there is nothing to attach to.
  if gh release view "$tag" --repo "$repo" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "release create failed but $tag now exists — lost the view→create race, the winner owns the release"
    echo "✅ lazy draft ready for $tag (owner $identity) — publish is provenance-owned (gh-1801)"
    exit 0
  fi
  echo "::error::the draft create for $tag failed (rc $create_rc) and no concurrent release appeared — nothing to attach to; fix the create failure above (e.g. the release body exceeding the 125,000-character API cap, gh-237)" >&2
  exit 1
fi
echo "✅ lazy draft ready for $tag (owner $identity) — publish is provenance-owned (gh-1801)"

release-provenance:
    name: Sign release checksums
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [binaries, web-spa, build-extension]
    timeout-minutes: 10
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.binaries.result == 'success' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')) ||
      github.event_name == 'release')
    permissions:
      contents: write # upload SHA256SUMS(.sig) to the GitHub Release
    steps:
      # gh-814 r2: the trust-anchor drift gate below diffs the secret's public
      # key against the PEM embedded in site/install.sh — that file must be
      # present, so the signing job checks out the site/ tree.
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: Collect release assets
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          mkdir -p provenance
          gh release download "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" \
            --dir provenance --pattern 'fa-*'
          ls -l provenance

      # gh-1832: PUBLISH-BLOCKING required-assets gate. The single source of
      # truth is scripts/release_required_assets.txt, consumed by
      # scripts/assert_release_assets.sh. v1.0.635 published without
      # fa-extension.zip because the extension's only producer (the daily
      # build-macos.yml build-extension leg) attached it to a "latest+1"
      # draft while this train published the tagged release — every leg
      # green, nothing asserted the published set. A missing asset here
      # fails the release run loudly and leaves the release a DRAFT (the
      # previous release stays latest) instead of publishing a partial one.
      - name: Assert required release assets (gh-1832 gate)
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: bash scripts/assert_release_assets.sh "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}"

      - name: Build and sign SHA256SUMS
        env:
          FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY }}
        run: |
          cd provenance
          sha256sum fa-* > SHA256SUMS
          if [ -z "$FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY" ]; then
            echo "::error::FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY is not set — refusing to publish a release without signed checksums (SEC-07 #795, fail-closed). Set the repo secret with the release-signing private key."
            exit 1
          fi
          printf '%s' "$FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key"
          chmod 600 "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key"
          # The key never outlives the step — trap covers mid-step failure.
          trap 'rm -f "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key"' EXIT
          openssl dgst -sha256 -sign "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key" -out SHA256SUMS.sig SHA256SUMS
          # Self-check: the signature must verify against OUR OWN public key
          # before anything is uploaded.
          openssl rsa -in "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key" -pubout -out pub.pem 2>/dev/null
          openssl dgst -sha256 -verify pub.pem -signature SHA256SUMS.sig SHA256SUMS
          rm -f "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key"
          # gh-814 r2 trust-anchor drift gate (fail-closed): the public key
          # derived from the secret must equal the PEM embedded in
          # site/install.sh — otherwise every pinned installer would ship an
          # anchor that rejects this release's signed checksums.
          sed -n '/BEGIN PUBLIC KEY/,/END PUBLIC KEY/p' "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/site/install.sh" |
            sed "1s/^.*BEGIN/-----BEGIN/; \$s/END.*\$/END PUBLIC KEY-----/" > embedded-anchor.pem
          openssl pkey -pubin -in embedded-anchor.pem -noout ||
            { echo "::error::site/install.sh trust anchor does not parse as a public key — regenerate installers (dart run scripts/gen_installers.dart)"; exit 1; }
          cmp embedded-anchor.pem pub.pem ||
            { echo "::error::FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY drifted from the trust anchor embedded in site/install.sh — rotate the keypair: update install.signing_public_key in site/install-config.yaml, regenerate installers, and update the repo secret TOGETHER. Refusing to sign (fail-closed)."; exit 1; }
          rm -f pub.pem embedded-anchor.pem

      - name: Upload provenance assets
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          gh release upload "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" \
            provenance/SHA256SUMS provenance/SHA256SUMS.sig \
            --clobber --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"
          # gh-1801 (rework): THE publish point of the train. The release
          # now carries every fa-* asset AND the signed SHA256SUMS(.sig) —
          # the first moment `fa update` can actually serve it (it
          # hard-fails without the signed checksums, bin/self_manage.dart).
          # Flip draft=false + latest here and ONLY here: a red provenance
          # leaves the previous release as latest (safe degradation)
          # instead of stranding a provenance-less one (the v1.0.630
          # empty/partial-latest window class).
          #
          # gh-2042 (BLOCKING review thread): the flip must never drag the
          # `latest` badge backwards. The drift remediation
          # (scripts/release_drift_remediate.sh) re-requests THIS job for
          # an old drifted tag; a job rerun re-executes this step with the
          # original run's ref, and an unconditional --latest would
          # re-flag that older release as Latest — pointing every
          # `fa update` client DOWN at it (the re-signed manifest would
          # make the downgrade pass provenance). Carry --latest ONLY when
          # the release is still a draft (the normal publish point,
          # gh-1801) or already the current latest; otherwise publish the
          # re-signed state without touching the badge.
          is_draft=$(gh release view "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --json isDraft --jq .isDraft)
          current_latest=$(gh api "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/releases/latest" --jq .tag_name 2>/dev/null || true)
          if [ "$is_draft" = "true" ] || [ "$current_latest" = "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" ]; then
            gh release edit "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" --draft=false --latest --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"
          else
            # Re-sign remediation of a non-latest tag: publish state is
            # already correct — never drag the latest badge backwards
            # (gh-2042).
            gh release edit "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" --draft=false --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"
          fi

      # gh-1899: the flip above publishes exactly ONE release object, but
      # GitHub does not atomically enforce one release per tag — two train
      # legs racing the lazy draft create can BOTH succeed (v1.0.641, run
      # 40163369302: twin drafts 87 ms apart), and the unpicked twin then
      # rots until the 24h sweeper deletes it and files a recurring sweep
      # issue. The tag is published and servable now: reclaim this run's
      # twin drafts. Success-path only — a red provenance keeps the draft
      # as the rerun --failed recovery vessel.
      # Best-effort by design (gh-1899 review): the flip above already
      # published the release — a cleanup-only API blip here must NOT fail
      # the provenance job (release-asset-smoke gates on its result and
      # would silently skip for a release that is actually fine). Warn
      # and stay green; the 24h sweeper remains the backstop.
      - name: Reclaim orphaned draft twins (gh-1899)
        if: success()
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: bash scripts/release_draft_dedupe.sh "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" || echo "::warning::gh-1899 twin-draft dedupe failed — the 24h sweeper remains the backstop"

  # Train-level draft lifecycle guard (issue #282, gh-2230): this train is
  # the PUBLISH OWNER of every staged draft (gh-1801 rework —
  # release-provenance above is the sole --draft=false --latest flip), but
  # the per-creating-job guards cover only their own job's failure. A train
  # that dies upstream of the publish point (core tests → quality-gate red
  # → binaries skipped → release-provenance SKIPPED) used to orphan the
  # staged draft: the creating run's jobs all succeeded (their guards never
  # fire), the failed train is superseded and never rerun, and
  # verify_pubdev_release.sh heals the LATEST tag only — so the draft rotted
  # exactly 24h until the daily sweeper deleted it and filed the recurring
  # sweep issue (gh-2230, v1.0.728). This job runs AFTER the publish point
  # settled — needs release-provenance + always(), so it fires on failed AND
  # cancelled trains and never on the success path's result (the script
  # no-ops on a published release). The script deletes ONLY when the
  # publish point is unreachable (result == 'skipped' — rerun --failed
  # never resurrects skipped jobs): drafts for THIS train's tag whose
  # owner-marker run has completed (scripts/release_train_draft_guard.sh).
  # A failed/cancelled provenance is rerunnable, so the staged draft stays
  # as the rerun --failed recovery vessel (gh-1899 convention). In-flight
  # owner runs and unmarked/human drafts stay with the sweeper (E1).
  train-draft-guard:

build-macos-cli:
    name: Build macOS CLI ${{ matrix.arch }}
    needs: version
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    # Ceiling for the daily cli watcher's budget arithmetic (#351): dart
    # CLI bundle + release upload; the two arches run in PARALLEL on
    # GitHub-hosted runners (they do not serialize like the self-hosted
    # build-macos matrix does).
    timeout-minutes: 45
    if: inputs.create_release == 'true'
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - runner: macos-latest
            arch: arm64
          - runner: macos-15-intel
            arch: x64
    permissions:
      contents: write
      # gh-2026: defense-in-depth for the release_tag_mint.sh
      # train-verification probe (`gh run list` on the tag ref); the
      # probe itself authenticates with RELEASE_PAT (gh prefers
      # GH_TOKEN, which every mint-reachable call site exports), so
      # this grant matters only if the probe is ever switched to the
      # job token. Granted on every mint-reachable job.
      actions: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # Blobless full history: the lazy draft create (gh-1801 rework)
          # builds the release body via scripts/release_notes.sh — same
          # reason as release-macos's checkout (gh-1477: the notes read
          # commit MESSAGES, never historical file blobs).
          fetch-depth: 0
          filter: blob:none

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@2286a0c042b44434fe26d292bbce8d34f7ec662b # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - run: dart pub get

      # gh-2075 (round-3 review): the hosted CLI lane runs on fresh GitHub
      # workspaces — pair the pre-warm with the hooks-shared restore (the
      # pinned ci.yml/build-mobile.yml hosted-lane pattern): a warm cache
      # reports "0 fetched, N already verified" with zero egress, so a
      # brownout window cannot touch the leg at all. Hardened like ci.yml
      # (timeout + continue-on-error): a cache-service hiccup degrades to
      # the pre-warm download path, never a red leg from the restore.
      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-
        timeout-minutes: 2
        continue-on-error: true

      # gh-2075 (run 42566734746): `dart build cli` triggers the
      # package:sqlite3 native-assets hook, which downloads its prebuilt
      # dylib with ONE un-retried GET — this leg died on a 504 Gateway
      # Time-out. Pre-warm the hook's digest-checked cache with the ONE
      # shared prewarm BEFORE the build: a flaky egress window fails here
      # in seconds, retried, instead of killing the bundle leg; the hook
      # re-validates any cached file against the same pinned digest, so
      # pre-warming is integrity-neutral.
      # gh-2105: the shared composite (gh-2072's ONE prewarm
      # implementation) replaces the retired inline 3-attempt script whose
      # ~3.5 min budget did not cover the 5+ minute v1.0.697 egress storm
      # that red'd this leg on the raw 504 (run 42566734746). Targets are
      # per-arch in the script's <abi>-<os> grammar; package-roots is the
      # root package this job resolves (dart pub get at the repo root),
      # declared explicitly next to the explicit targets. Best-effort
      # semantics live inside the composite (a failed prewarm degrades to
      # the hook's own single-attempt download, never reds the leg).
      - name: Prewarm sqlite3 native-assets (gh-2075, composite contract)
        uses: ./.github/actions/sqlite3-native-assets-prewarm
        with:
          targets: ${{ matrix.arch }}-macos
          package-roots: .

      - name: Build CLI bundle
        run: |
          version="${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}"
          # gh-2120 follow-up: the entry is BUILT as `fa` (bin/fa.dart), not
          # renamed — on Dart >=3.14 (native linux) the bundle is split
          # (thin launcher + libdartaot<exe>.so) and a post-build mv
          # desyncs the pair (`dartaotruntime: not an AOT snapshot`).
          dart build cli --target=bin/fa.dart --output=build/out
          chmod +x build/out/bundle/bin/fa
          echo "$version" > build/out/bundle/version.txt

      - name: Ad-hoc sign CLI binary
        run: |
          codesign --force --sign - build/out/bundle/bin/fa

      # gh-2040: the native fa-clip pasteboard helper rides the macOS CLI
      # bundle (bundle/bin/fa-clip, per-arch — this matrix builds each arch
      # on a native runner, AC8) so install.sh / fa update ship it beside
      # the binary and image paste never rides Apple Events.
      - name: Build fa-clip pasteboard helper (gh-2040)
        run: |
          bash scripts/build_fa_clip.sh build/out/bundle/bin/fa-clip
          codesign --force --sign - build/out/bundle/bin/fa-clip
          test -x build/out/bundle/bin/fa-clip

      - name: Archive and upload CLI bundle
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT }}
          RELEASE_TAG: ${{ needs.version.outputs.tag }}
          # Matrix legs share GITHUB_JOB=build-macos-cli — the leg-suffixed
          # draft owner identity keeps the guard below scoped to the leg
          # that created the draft, never the sibling's mid-upload one.
          RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY: run/${{ github.run_id }}/job/${{ github.job }}-${{ matrix.arch }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          asset="fa-macos-${{ matrix.arch }}.tar.gz"
          tar -czf "$asset" -C build/out bundle
          ls -lh "$asset"

          # gh-1801 (rework): DRAFT-first, publish is PROVENANCE-OWNED.
          # The CLI tarball is a `fa update` asset, but servability needs
          # the SIGNED SHA256SUMS — which only the tag-run's
          # release-provenance job uploads (ci.yml). So: create the draft
          # lazily (curated notes via release_notes.sh + THIS leg's
          # draft-owner marker the guard below can reclaim), upload, and
          # let provenance own the --draft=false --latest flip.
          bash scripts/release_lazy_draft.sh "$RELEASE_TAG"
          # gh-2042 AC1: the immutability gate owns the attach — a
          # PUBLISHED release (the same-tag convergence race) skips
          # attached assets and refuses unattached fa-* assets loud
          # instead of silently drifting the signed SHA256SUMS.
          bash scripts/release_asset_gate.sh "$RELEASE_TAG" "$asset"

      # Draft lifecycle invariant (issue #282): this job creates releases,
      # so a failed/cancelled run must not leave one behind as a draft.
      # Leg-scoped (gh-1801): matches only THIS arch leg's marker.
      - name: Draft lifecycle guard (delete orphaned draft on failure)
        if: always() && job.status != 'success'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT }}
          RELEASE_TAG: ${{ needs.version.outputs.tag }}
          RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY: run/${{ github.run_id }}/job/${{ github.job }}-${{ matrix.arch }}
        run: bash scripts/release_draft_guard.sh "$RELEASE_TAG"

## Development Mode: Plan (plan-mode protocol appendix)

This leg runs in **plan mode**: work through an explicit, committed task
plan instead of free-form execution. Everything else in the instruction
pack still applies unchanged — this appendix only structures HOW you work.
`<KEY>` below is the current ticket key.

### 1. Decompose before editing

- Before writing any production code, break the ticket into numbered tasks
  `T1..Tn` in `outputs/<KEY>/plan.md` (the working copy).
- Every task carries exactly two fields:
  - `what` — the concrete change this task makes;
  - `verify` — how to check it passed (the command to run and the expected
    result).
- End the plan with two sections:
  - `## Decisions` — the chosen approach for every open point;
  - `## Open questions` — anything unresolved, with the workaround you picked.

### 2. Mirror the plan into a committed snapshot

- Mirror the plan to `.dmtools/plan-snapshot.md` and commit it on the dev
  branch right away: commit subject `<KEY>: plan`.
- The snapshot — not the working copy — is the durable artifact: it survives
  interruption windows and CI session-cache loss. (`outputs/` never rides
  commits.)
- When a task completes: mark its checkbox `[x]` in BOTH files and commit
  the snapshot update: `<KEY>: plan update T# done` (one commit per task).
- The periodic WIP auto-save commits keep running as usual; your plan
  commits coexist with them.

### 3. Resume rule (continuation legs)

- At leg start: if a plan file (`outputs/<KEY>/plan.md` or
  `.dmtools/plan-snapshot.md`) already exists, or the branch already carries
  commits, this leg is a CONTINUATION, not a fresh start:
  1. Read the plan and `git log`.
  2. Reconcile the plan checkboxes against the actual branch diff — a task
     whose change is already on the branch is done, checkbox or not.
  3. Execute ONLY the still-pending tasks.

### 4. Close out — the plan file never rides the pull request

- When the LAST task is done (every checkbox `[x]`), remove the snapshot
  from the branch again: `git rm .dmtools/plan-snapshot.md`, commit
  subject `<KEY>: plan done`.
- Do this BEFORE writing `outputs/<KEY>/response.md`: the completion
  report is the leg's deliverable — the plan file is leg scaffolding.
- The engine repeats this cleanup defensively before the PR is created,
  so an open pull request never carries the plan file.

# Root Cause Analysis — gh-2372 `[daily-publish] stale release drafts swept`

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: The daily draft sweeper swept a "stale pipeline-created draft" `v1.0.760` and filed the recurring `[daily-publish] stale release drafts swept` issue, even though release v1.0.760 itself was published successfully by a green train — nothing had died.

**Root cause**: `scripts/release_lazy_draft.sh`'s view→create race is not idempotent for DRAFT objects. Inside one `build-macos.yml` run, three sibling jobs (`build-macos-cli-arm64`, `build-macos-cli-x64`, `build-extension`) call `release_lazy_draft.sh` concurrently against the same derived tag. When their view/create calls interleave inside the race window (production: the same second), **both `gh release create --draft` calls succeed** — GitHub does not enforce one-release-per-tag for drafts (the gh-1899 v1.0.641 precedent) — and two twin drafts are born. The tag train's `release-provenance` flips exactly ONE object to published; the twin rots.

**Production evidence** (IstiN/flutter_agent_harness, queried live):

| release | object | owner marker | created_at | state |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| v1.0.760 (gh-2372) | 453463937 | `run/44870476733/job/build-extension` | 2026-11-21T05:29:27Z | published 06:06:42Z by the green train |
| v1.0.760 twin (swept) | — | `run/44870476733/job/…` (per the sweep issue's creating-run link) | 2026-11-21T05:29:27Z | same run, same second → the sibling `build-macos-cli` leg; rotted 43h, swept by the gh-2372 sweep |
| v1.0.763 (live at RCA time) | 454339894 | `run/45007933749/job/build-macos-cli-arm64` | 2026-11-22T09:38:51Z | published 10:07:20Z |
| v1.0.763 twin (live) | 454339915 | `run/45007933749/job/build-extension` | 2026-11-22T09:38:51Z | still a draft, ZERO assets — the gh-2372 sweep itself counted it "fresh: 1" |

The twin's zero assets prove the shape: `release_lazy_draft.sh` attaches nothing (the caller uploads by tag afterwards, which resolves the winner), so the loser object is born empty and stays empty.

**Why every existing guard misses it**:

1. `scripts/release_draft_guard.sh` (per-job failure path) — never fires: all creating jobs SUCCEEDED.
2. `scripts/release_draft_dedupe.sh` (train-side, post-publish) — reclaims only twins stamped with the **train's** `GITHUB_RUN_ID`; child-run twins carry the build-macos run's id. The v1.0.760 train log says exactly this: "nothing to reclaim for v1.0.760 (no own-run twin drafts)".
3. `scripts/release_train_draft_guard.sh` (gh-2230) — fires only when `release-provenance` is SKIPPED (publish unreachable); here the train succeeded.
4. `scripts/sweep_stale_drafts.sh` — deletes the rotted twin >24h later and files the recurring issue, with the generic prose "a `gh release create` step died between asset upload and publish — check the creating run's failed step". Misleading: creating run 44870476733 succeeded (conclusion success, verified).

**Impact**: No user-facing release breakage (the winner publishes and serves `fa update`), but every same-second sibling race rots a zero-asset twin for ≥24h, re-files the recurring sweep issue, and points the diagnosis at a "failed step" that does not exist. v1.0.763's live twin re-files the issue on the next daily sweep (it goes stale at 2026-11-23T09:38:51Z, sweep 2026-11-24T05:17Z). Recurrence confirmed: same shape on 11-21 and 11-22.

**Fix approach** (two layers, issue #282's "published or deleted — never orphaned" invariant closed for the success path):

1. **At the source** — after a successful draft create, the creator self-deletes its OWN just-created draft (exact `release-draft-owner` marker match, delete by id — never tag-based) when an OLDER pipeline-created release for the same tag exists (draft or published). Winner election is deterministic: lowest release id (= first-created) keeps the tag; the loser's caller then attaches into the winner by tag — making gh-1801's tolerated contract ("the loser just uploads into the winner's release") actually true. New `scripts/release_draft_twin_dedupe.sh`, wired after the successful creates in `release_lazy_draft.sh` and `release_attach_or_create.sh`. Best-effort (warn, never red a green leg) — the sweeper remains the backstop, per the gh-1899 dedupe convention.
2. **Sweeper backstop** — a FRESH marker draft whose tag already carries a PUBLISHED release is a proven orphan (nothing can ever publish or attach into it; uploads resolve the published object), so the sweep reclaims it immediately as routine hygiene (gh-236 pattern: reported in the summary, not a sweep finding — a residual twin must not re-file the issue). The sweep prose also names the twin shape when the deleted draft's creating run concluded success, instead of the misleading "step died" text.

**Previous attempt**: none for this shape. gh-1899's dedupe covers train-run twins only; gh-2318's fresh reclaim covers the failed-train shape only. Neither covers same-run child twins under a SUCCEEDED train — that is the missing lifecycle guard this ticket's prose points at ("Recurrence means a lifecycle guard is missing (issue #282)").

# gh-2372 — plan (plan-mode protocol)

Root cause (see outputs/rca.md): same-run sibling jobs racing `release_lazy_draft.sh` /
`release_attach_or_create.sh` create twin drafts (both `gh release create --draft` succeed);
the train publishes one, the twin rots 24h+ and re-files the recurring sweep issue.
Fix = source-side self-dedupe + sweeper backstop + truthful prose.

## Tasks

- [ ] T1 — RED: reproduction tests for the twin race
  - what: new `test/release_draft_twin_dedupe_test.dart` (behavioral, stateful gh stub in the
    release_hygiene support style): (a) lazy-draft loser self-deletes its own twin when an older
    pipeline draft owns the tag, (b) winner keeps its draft, (c) a human (unmarked) older draft
    never triggers a self-delete and never gets deleted, (d) `release_attach_or_create.sh`'
    create path self-dedupes the same way, (e) wiring proof: both creator scripts invoke
    `release_draft_twin_dedupe.sh` right after their successful creates.
  - verify: `dart test test/release_draft_twin_dedupe_test.dart` — new tests FAIL (script missing /
    twin survives) before T2.
- [ ] T2 — GREEN: the source guard
  - what: new `scripts/release_draft_twin_dedupe.sh <tag>` — lists releases (paginated), finds
    same-tag releases; if any OLDER (lower id) pipeline-created one exists (published, or draft
    with a well-formed `release-draft-owner: run/<id>/job/<name>` marker / bot author / machine
    account), deletes the draft carrying THIS job's exact marker by release id, warns, exits 0.
    Fail-safe: unmarked/mine-not-found/older-draft-is-human → keep, exit 0. Wire the call after
    the successful creates in `release_lazy_draft.sh` and `release_attach_or_create.sh`.
  - verify: `dart test test/release_draft_twin_dedupe_test.dart` and the existing
    `test/release_lazy_draft_mint_test.dart`, `test/release_attach_or_create_mint_test.dart`,
    `test/release_draft_dedupe_test.dart`, `test/release_hygiene_test.dart`,
    `test/release_stale_draft_reclaim_test.dart` all PASS.
- [ ] T3 — sweeper backstop + truthful prose (RED→GREEN)
  - what: in `scripts/sweep_stale_drafts.sh`: (a) fresh-marker-draft branch — when the tag already
    has a PUBLISHED release, reclaim the twin immediately as routine hygiene (new non-finding
    counter + gh-236-style summary/issue section); (b) when a stale bot-bucket draft's creating
    run (marker run id) concluded success, name the twin shape instead of the misleading
    "gh release create step died" prose. Tests in `test/release_stale_draft_reclaim_test.dart`
    (or a sibling file) following the runSweeper fixture style.
  - verify: new sweeper tests pass; all existing sweeper/hygiene tests pass unchanged
    (`dart test test/release_hygiene_test.dart test/release_stale_draft_reclaim_test.dart`).
- [ ] T4 — full verification + docs + outputs
  - what: run the full release-related test set + `dart analyze` on touched files + format;
    check `docs/ci.md` for a draft-lifecycle section to update (one paragraph: twins now
    self-deduped at create + sweeper reclaims fresh twins whose tag is published). Write
    `outputs/gh-2372/response.md`, git status review.
  - verify: `dart test test/release_*` green; `dart analyze` clean; `dart format` no changes;
    git status shows only intended files; completion post-check.

## Decisions

- Winner election: lowest release id (first-created) wins; losers self-delete by exact
  release id. Ids are monotonic, so the later creator always sees the earlier one — no
  interleaving can make both keep a twin.
- "Pipeline-created" = well-formed `release-draft-owner: run/<id>/job/<name>` marker in the body,
  or author.type == Bot / login ends [bot] / login == DAILY_PUBLISH_ASSIGNEE — the sweeper's
  exact bucket rule (gh-2287/gh-236), kept consistent.
- Self-delete requires the draft to carry THIS job's exact marker (identity discipline of
  release_draft_guard.sh) — a job can only ever delete what it just created.
- Human/unmarked older same-tag drafts never trigger self-delete (E1) and are never deleted by
  the new script; the twin-vs-human ambiguity is pre-existing and out of scope.
- Best-effort semantics (warn + exit 0 on cleanup failure): matches release_draft_dedupe.sh's
  gh-1899 review convention; a cleanup blip must not red a green leg whose draft is harmless.
- Sweeper twin reclaim is non-finding (gh-236 artefact-cache precedent): visible in summary +
  issue-when-open, never files/comments a NEW issue; the source guard makes residual twins
  best-effort-failure leftovers only.
- No changes to ci.yml / build-macos.yml workflows needed: the guard lives in the two creator
  scripts every create path already goes through.

## Open questions

- None blocking. (Checked: `docs/ci.md` documents the draft lifecycle — T4 updates it.)

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
# ║  QUALITY GATE — DO NOT LOWER THESE THRESHOLDS WITHOUT TEAM APPROVAL       ║
# ║  Every commit must pass: file size (crap4dart loc), analyze, tests,       ║
# ║  coverage ≥ 80%, CRAP ratchet (crap4dart.yaml), duplication < 1%.         ║
# ╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
#
# Pre-commit hook for flutter_agent_harness (pure Dart package).
# Canonical copy: scripts/pre-commit — install with:
#   cp scripts/pre-commit .git/hooks/pre-commit && chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit
# To skip (emergency only): git commit --no-verify
#
# Issue #177 (AC7): the hook is a THIN WRAPPER over scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh —
# the exact script CI runs — with the same path filters: a docs-only commit
# no longer pays for the flutter suite, a lib-only commit skips flutter_app
# stages. Hook-specific extras that stay here (they make no sense in CI):
#   1. dart format SELF-HEAL of staged files (reformat + re-stage, blocking
#      backstop when the formatter can't),
#   2. the golden-coverage quick check (check_goldens.py --quick) — local
#      golden hygiene; pixel goldens themselves run inside the gate's
#      flutter stage.
# Parity check: both callers print `GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP <reason>`
# markers; diffing the hook's markers against CI's must be empty.

set -euo pipefail

cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"

echo "🎨 Auto-formatting staged Dart files..."
# Format is SELF-HEALING with a BLOCKING backstop: reformat exactly the
# Dart files in the index and re-stage them; anything still unformatted
# after that (formatter crashed on syntax errors) blocks the commit with a
# clear message. A whole-tree `--set-exit-if-changed` gate both (a) failed
# commits over a single unformatted line and (b) rewrote OTHER agents'
# work-in-progress files mid-edit when run concurrently — scoped auto-fix
# avoids both.
STAGED_DART=$(git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACM | grep '\.dart$' || true)
if [ -n "$STAGED_DART" ]; then

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Post-create twin-draft self-dedupe (gh-2372) — the success-path half of
# the issue #282 invariant for CHILD-run drafts.
#
# Why this exists: the view→create race between sibling jobs of ONE
# release run is NOT benign for DRAFT objects. GitHub does not enforce
# one release per tag for drafts (gh-1899, v1.0.641: twin drafts 87 ms
# apart), so when two legs of the same build-macos.yml run hit the race
# window — production: the SAME SECOND (v1.0.760: build-extension won +
# was published, its build-macos-cli twin rotted 43h and was swept by
# gh-2372; v1.0.763: build-macos-cli-arm64 won, the build-extension twin
# is a live zero-asset draft) — BOTH `gh release create --draft` calls
# succeed and two twin drafts are born. The tag train publishes exactly
# ONE object; the twin rots until the daily sweeper deletes it and
# re-files the recurring "[daily-publish] stale release drafts swept"
# issue. No existing guard fires: every creating job SUCCEEDED (the
# failure-path guards never run), and release_draft_dedupe.sh matches
# only twins stamped with the TRAIN's GITHUB_RUN_ID — child-run twins
# carry the build-macos run's id and are invisible to it.
#
# This closes the race at the source. Call it RIGHT AFTER a successful
# draft create (release_lazy_draft.sh + release_attach_or_create.sh):
#
#   - OUR draft = a same-tag DRAFT whose body carries EXACTLY this job's
#     ownership marker (release-draft-owner: run/<id>/job/<name>, the
#     stampers' exact shape; capture + full-value equality, so run/111
#     can never match run/1111 — the release_draft_guard.sh discipline).
#     A job can only ever delete the draft(s) it just created.
#   - WINNER ELECTION (deterministic): the OLDEST same-tag release wins —
#     ids are monotonic, so the first-created object always has the
#     lowest id and a later creator always sees it in its listing; no
#     interleaving can make both jobs keep a twin. The winner is any
#     older same-tag release that is PUBLISHED (the train already flipped
#     the sibling) or PIPELINE-created: a well-formed
#     release-draft-owner marker in the body, author.type == Bot, a
#     *[bot] login, or the machine account (DAILY_PUBLISH_ASSIGNEE —
#     the sweeper's exact gh-2287 bucket rule, kept consistent).
#   - When a winner exists, every draft carrying OUR exact marker is
#     deleted BY ID via the API — never a tag-based delete (drafts may
#     carry an empty tag_name; under duplicate releases a tag lookup is
#     ambiguous — the very class this guards). The caller then attaches
#     into the winner by tag — release_lazy_draft's gh-1801 contract
#     "the loser just uploads into the winner's release", now actually
#     true.
#   - HUMAN drafts (unmarked, User author) never win and never trigger a
#     self-delete (E1): the pipeline must not ride a human draft, and a
#     human draft must never be deleted by automation. Our draft stays
#     and is reclaimed by the 24h sweeper as today.
#   - BEST-EFFORT (gh-1899 review convention): every failure here — the
#     listing blips, one failed DELETE — warns and exits 0. The call
#     site is a green create path; a cleanup blip must never red a leg
#     whose leftover is harmless (the sweeper remains the backstop, and
#     sweep_stale_drafts.sh reclaims fresh twins whose tag is already
#     published). Only a malformed RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY fails loud —
#     the marker-stamping scripts already validate it pre-create; a
#     marker nothing could ever match is a configuration bug, not a
#     cleanup blip.
#
# Usage: release_draft_twin_dedupe.sh <tag>
# Env: GITHUB_REPOSITORY, GITHUB_RUN_ID, GITHUB_JOB (Actions defaults),
#      RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY (optional leg-suffixed override, same as
#      release_lazy_draft.sh / release_draft_guard.sh),
#      DAILY_PUBLISH_ASSIGNEE (default ai-teammate), GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN.
set -euo pipefail

tag="${1:?usage: release_draft_twin_dedupe.sh <tag>}"
repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:?GITHUB_REPOSITORY must be set}"
identity="${RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY:-run/${GITHUB_RUN_ID:?GITHUB_RUN_ID must be set (GitHub Actions default env)}/job/${GITHUB_JOB:?GITHUB_JOB must be set (GitHub Actions default env)}}"
assignee="${DAILY_PUBLISH_ASSIGNEE:-ai-teammate}"

printf '%s' "$identity" | grep -Eq '^run/[0-9]+/job/[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$' || {
  echo "::error::RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY '$identity' does not match 'run/<id>/job/<name>' — the marker we stamped could never be matched by any guard" >&2
  exit 1
}

# One paginated listing answers both questions (ours + winner). A blip
# degrades to keep — never judge twins off a partial roster.
list=$(gh api --paginate "repos/$repo/releases" 2>/dev/null) || {
  echo "::warning::release twin dedupe: the release listing failed — cannot judge twins, keeping our draft for $tag" >&2
  exit 0
}

# Same-tag drafts carrying EXACTLY our marker (capture + full-value
# equality — the prefix trap release_draft_guard.sh pins: run/111/job/x
# must never match run/1111/job/x or run/111/job/x-longer).
mine_ids=$(printf '%s' "$list" | jq -s -r --arg tag "$tag" --arg id "$identity" '
  [ flatten[]
    | select(.draft == true and .tag_name == $tag)
    | select((((.body // "")
        | (capture("release-draft-owner: (?<m>run/[0-9]+/job/[A-Za-z0-9_-]+)")? | .m) // "")
        == $id))
    | .id | tostring ]
  | unique | .[]')

if [ -z "$mine_ids" ]; then
  echo "release twin dedupe: no own draft for $tag in the listing — nothing to clean"
  exit 0
fi

# Deterministic winner: any older (lower id — first-created) same-tag
# release that is published or pipeline-created.
mine_min=$(printf '%s\n' "$mine_ids" | sort -n | head -1)
winner=$(printf '%s' "$list" | jq -s -r --arg tag "$tag" --arg assignee "$assignee" --argjson mine "$mine_min" '
  [ flatten[]
    | select(.tag_name == $tag and .id < $mine)
    | select(.draft == false
        or ((.author.type // "User") == "Bot")
        or ((.author.login // "") | test("\\[bot\\]$"))
        or ((.author.login // "") == $assignee)
        or ((.body // "") | test("release-draft-owner: run/[0-9]+/job/[A-Za-z0-9_-]+"))) ]
  | length > 0')

if [ "$winner" != "true" ]; then
  echo "release twin dedupe: our draft for $tag is the oldest same-tag release — it stays"
  exit 0
fi

deleted=0
while IFS= read -r id; do
  [ -n "$id" ] || continue
  if gh api -X DELETE "repos/$repo/releases/$id" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    deleted=$((deleted + 1))
  else
    echo "::warning::release twin dedupe: deleting our twin draft $id for $tag failed — the daily sweeper reclaims it (fresh twins whose tag is published are reclaimed immediately; gh-2372)" >&2
  fi
done <<< "$mine_ids"

if [ "$deleted" -gt 0 ]; then
  echo "::warning::release twin dedupe: deleted $deleted own twin draft(s) for $tag — an older release already owns the tag (the same-run sibling create race, gh-2372); the caller attaches into the winner by tag (gh-1801 tolerance), nothing was lost: the twin carried only our unpublished assets" >&2
fi
exit 0

create_rc=0
gh release create "$tag" \
  --repo "$repo" \
  --title "$tag" \
  --draft \
  --notes-file "$notes_file" || create_rc=$?
if [ "$create_rc" -eq 0 ]; then
  # gh-2372: the create SUCCEEDED, but a same-run sibling leg may have
  # created its own draft inside the view→create race window (GitHub
  # does not enforce one release per tag for drafts — the v1.0.760 /
  # v1.0.763 twin rot). The older (first-created) same-tag release must
  # win: self-delete OUR twin when we lost, so the caller attaches into
  # the winner and nothing rots for 24h until the sweeper. Best-effort.
  bash "$(dirname "$0")/release_draft_twin_dedupe.sh" "$tag"
  echo "✅ lazy draft ready for $tag (owner $identity) — publish is provenance-owned (gh-1801)"
  exit 0
fi
if [ "$create_rc" -ne 0 ]; then
  # gh-1801's `|| true` tolerated ONLY the view→create race — a sibling
  # leg creating the release between our view and create. gh-237 (run
  # 44680647719, v1.0.756): that swallow ALSO ate real create failures
  # (body-too-long 422), printed "✅ lazy draft ready", and failed every
  # attach gate with "release not found". Re-view: the release existing
  # NOW means we lost the race (upload into the winner's release); it
  # still being missing means the create itself failed — the leg must
  # go red, there is nothing to attach to.
  if gh release view "$tag" --repo "$repo" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "release create failed but $tag now exists — lost the view→create race, the winner owns the release"
    echo "✅ lazy draft ready for $tag (owner $identity) — publish is provenance-owned (gh-1801)"
    exit 0
  fi
  echo "::error::the draft create for $tag failed (rc $create_rc) and no concurrent release appeared — nothing to attach to; fix the create failure above (e.g. the release body exceeding the 125,000-character API cap, gh-237)" >&2
  exit 1
fi

issue)
    if [ "\$2" = "list" ]; then
      # gh-2359: the run-id join query (--json number,body --jq ... --arg
      # run_url ...) is served from issues-body.json through the real jq.
      if printf '%s' "\$*" | grep -q 'number,body'; then
        jqf="."; argn=""; argv=""
        while [ \$# -gt 0 ]; do
          case "\$1" in
            --jq) jqf="\$2"; shift 2 ;;
            --arg) argn="\$2"; argv="\$3"; shift 3 ;;
            *) shift ;;
          esac
        done
        if [ -s "\$GH_STUB_DIR/issues-body.json" ]; then
          if [ -n "\$argn" ]; then
            jq -r --arg "\$argn" "\$argv" "\$jqf" "\$GH_STUB_DIR/issues-body.json"
          else
            jq -r "\$jqf" "\$GH_STUB_DIR/issues-body.json"
          fi
        else
          echo '[]' | jq -r "\$jqf"
        fi
        exit 0
      fi
      cat "\$GH_STUB_DIR/issues.tsv" 2>/dev/null || true; exit 0
    fi
    want_url=""
    [ "\$2" = "create" ] && want_url=1
    while [ \$# -gt 0 ]; do
      if [ "\$1" = "--body-file" ]; then
        cp "\$2" "\$GH_STUB_DIR/last-body.md" 2>/dev/null || true
      fi
      shift
    done
    [ -n "\$want_url" ] && echo "https://github.com/OWNER/REPO/issues/13"
    ;;
  release)
    case "\$2" in
      view)
        # Scripted view sequence for the attach-or-create tests: one word
        # per call (exists|missing), popped off the top. An EXHAUSTED
        # (empty) sequence file falls through to the structured answers —
        # the gh-1801 rework adds a servability query (assets) after the
        # scripted exists/missing verdicts.
        if [ -s "\$GH_STUB_DIR/view-seq.txt" ]; then
          w=\$(head -1 "\$GH_STUB_DIR/view-seq.txt")
          sed -i.bak '1d' "\$GH_STUB_DIR/view-seq.txt" && rm -f "\$GH_STUB_DIR/view-seq.txt.bak"
          [ "\$w" = "exists" ] && exit 0
          # gh-2042: an 'error' word models an API blip (rc != 0, stderr
          # without a "not found" verdict) — the indeterminable state the
          # immutability gate must fail CLOSED on.
          [ "\$w" = "error" ] && { echo "gh: HTTP 502 (stub API blip)" >&2; exit 1; }
          echo "release not found (stub)" >&2
          exit 1
        fi
        case " \$*" in
        # gh-2042: the immutability gate asks isDraft+assets in ONE call —
        # serve both from the fixture. Absent release-state.txt defaults to
        # DRAFT: the historical attach fixtures model a draft release (the
        # pre-gate behavior every existing test pins). Published paths plant
        # release-state.txt=false explicitly.
        *--json\\ isDraft,assets*)
          st="true"
          [ -s "\$GH_STUB_DIR/release-state.txt" ] && st="\$(cat "\$GH_STUB_DIR/release-state.txt")"
          objs=""
          if [ -s "\$GH_STUB_DIR/asset-names.txt" ]; then
            while IFS= read -r n; do
              [ -n "\$n" ] && objs="\$objs{\\"name\\":\\"\$n\\"},"
            done < "\$GH_STUB_DIR/asset-names.txt"
          fi
          objs="\${objs%,}"
          printf '{"isDraft":%s,"assets":[%s]}\n' "\$st" "\$objs"

content.text:
No orphan drafts, one naming scheme, a truthful `Latest`, useful notes:

- **Draft lifecycle invariant** — every workflow step that creates a
  release draft (`gh release create <tag> <assets…>` uploads assets
  through a *draft* first and only publishes afterwards) is paired with a
  `Draft lifecycle guard` step in the same job:
  `if: always() && job.status != 'success'` + `scripts/release_draft_guard.sh`
  — a failed **or cancelled** run deletes its orphaned draft instead of
  leaving it to rot. The delete is **ownership-scoped** (review of #294):
  the guard only deletes a draft whose body carries this very run+job's
  `<!-- release-draft-owner: run/<id>/job/<job> -->` marker — daily-publish
  runs the mobile and macOS legs concurrently on the same derived tag, and
  a failed leg's guard must never destroy the sibling leg's mid-upload
  draft (foreign or unmarked drafts are left to the sweeper). Pinned by
  `test/release_hygiene_test.dart` (a job with an asset-carrying create
  and no guard fails CI).
- **Train-level draft lifecycle guard** (gh-2230) — the per-job guards
  above fire only on their own job's failure, but since the gh-1801
  rework the staged draft's publish owner is the TAG TRAIN (ci.yml's
  `release-provenance`, the sole publish point). A train that dies
  upstream of the publish point (core tests → quality-gate red → binaries
  skipped → provenance skipped) used to orphan the staged draft until the
  24h sweeper reclaimed it and filed the recurring sweep issue. ci.yml now
  carries a `train-draft-guard` job (`needs: release-provenance`,
  `if: always()` on tag-push/release events) running
  `scripts/release_train_draft_guard.sh` with the publish point's settled
  result exported. It deletes ONLY when that result is `skipped` (the
  publish point is unreachable — `rerun --failed` never resurrects skipped
  jobs): drafts for the trained tag whose well-formed ownership marker
  names a COMPLETED run go away (a superseded failed train is never rerun,
  so nobody else would ever publish them; the git tag is untouched). A
  FAILED or CANCELLED provenance is rerunnable, so the staged draft stays
  as the `rerun --failed` recovery vessel (gh-1899 convention). Fail-safe
  keeps — in-flight owner runs (a concurrent creator leg may be
  mid-upload), unmarked/human drafts (E1), any owner-status lookup failure
  (never delete blind), and an unexported result; the sweeper remains the
  backstop. Grants `contents: write` + `actions: read`, same
  stub-enforced model as the sweep-drafts job.
- **Attach-or-create** — the draft-capable creates of build-macos.yml /
  build-mobile.yml live in `scripts/release_attach_or_create.sh`, which is
  idempotent under the view→create race (#282 E3): a create that loses to
  a concurrent winner uploads into the winner's release instead of
  failing (a failing create would fire the guard against the winner's
  in-flight draft), and the create stamps the ownership marker the guard
  verifies.
- **Daily sweeper** — the `sweep-drafts` job in `daily-publish.yml` runs
  `scripts/sweep_stale_drafts.sh` on **every** daily invocation (leg
  results and change-gating never gate hygiene): drafts older than 24h
  are deleted when the PIPELINE created them — a Bot author / `*[bot]`
  login, or the body carries a well-formed
  `release-draft-owner: run/<id>/job/<job>` marker (the drafts
  are created with the owner's RELEASE_PAT, so the API author is a human
  and the marker is the only ownership proof — gh-2008; the bucket rule
  keys on the exact stamped shape, so prose merely mentioning the
  substring or a malformed marker stays human — review thread
  PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6yOzIh; id-based API
  delete, tag and git history untouched — draft assets are unpublished by
  definition, E2), human drafts (no marker) are listed but kept (E1),
  fresh (<24h) drafts are left for their in-flight run — EXCEPT the
  gh-2318 early reclaim: a fresh draft whose well-formed marker names a
  COMPLETED run is deleted immediately when no ci.yml push train on the

COMPLETED run is deleted immediately when no ci.yml push train on the
  tag is queued/in-flight and the tag's newest concluded ci.yml push train
  failed with release-provenance SKIPPED (the publish point is unreachable
  — `rerun --failed` cannot resurrect skipped jobs, so nobody will ever
  publish it; the same criterion as the gh-2230 train-draft-guard, which
  only sees drafts visible at train end). A rerunnable (FAILED) provenance
  keeps the draft as the `rerun --failed` recovery vessel (gh-1899) until
  it goes stale; an in-flight owner run, ANY queued/in-flight tag train
  (even with an older failed train), and any lookup failure keep too
  (never delete blind). The job grants
  `actions: read` — unmarked swept drafts name their creating run via
  `gh run list`, which 403s without it; marker drafts name the marker's
  run id directly. Anything
  stale files **one** deduplicated `release-hygiene` issue (comment on the
  open one, auto-close on a clean sweep — same convention as the leg
  issues) naming each swept draft and its creating run, so a recurring
  stuck draft points at its broken step. The test stub enforces the
  workflow-declared token permissions, so a dropped grant fails CI instead
  of silently degrading the issue to "no run on ref".
- **Artefact-cache lifecycle** (gh-236) — the machine loop writes every fa
  leg's session/output snapshots into a per-ticket DRAFT release
  `ai-gh-<n>` / `ai-pr-<n>` (dmtools-agents factory: `timerAutoCommitAndSave.js`
  → `releaseArtefacts.uploadRawFile` → `github_get_or_create_draft_release`,
  tag template `ai-{ticketKey}`), authored by ai-teammate with its own
  token — marker-less, no Actions run owns it. Those drafts are caches by
  design (never published), so the sweeper manages them by lifecycle, not
  as release failures: a machine-account draft whose tag matches
  `ai-(gh|pr)-<digits>` is **reclaimed immediately — any age — once its
  ticket entity is `closed`** (issues REST API serves PRs too; a closed
  cycle never resumes — a reopened ticket starts a fresh session, and the
  pack's restore is non-fatal, recreating the cache on "first run"), kept
  while the ticket is open and the draft is fresh (an in-flight leg may be
  writing snapshots), swept by the existing 24h backstop when the ticket
  stays open (parked leg), and kept on any ticket-state lookup failure
  (never delete blind) — only the 24h backstop then applies. The class is
  excluded from the sweep-issue finding
  counters — reclaiming a lifecycle-managed cache is routine hygiene, so

  auto-closes when only cache traffic remains. Human-authored `ai-*`

- **Attach-or-create** — the draft-capable creates of build-macos.yml /
  build-mobile.yml live in `scripts/release_attach_or_create.sh`, which is
  idempotent under the view→create race (#282 E3): a create that loses to
  a concurrent winner uploads into the winner's release instead of
  failing (a failing create would fire the guard against the winner's
  in-flight draft), and the create stamps the ownership marker the guard
  verifies.
- **Twin-draft self-dedupe** (gh-2372) — the view→create race above is
  NOT benign for drafts: GitHub does not enforce one release per tag for
  DRAFT objects, so two sibling legs of one run racing the window
  (production: the same second — v1.0.760's build-macos-cli twin vs its
  published build-extension sibling; v1.0.763's build-extension twin)
  BOTH create successfully. The train publishes exactly one; the twin
  rots 24h+ and re-files the recurring sweep issue with the misleading
  "a `gh release create` step died" prose (nothing died — every creating
  job succeeded, and `release_draft_dedupe.sh` matches only the TRAIN's
  own-run twins, so child-run twins were invisible to every guard). After
  a successful draft create, `release_lazy_draft.sh` and
  `release_attach_or_create.sh` now run
  `scripts/release_draft_twin_dedupe.sh <tag>`: when an OLDER (lower id =
  first-created) same-tag release exists that is published or
  pipeline-created (well-formed marker / Bot author / machine account),
  every draft carrying THIS job's exact ownership marker is deleted by id
  and the caller attaches into the winner by tag — the deterministic
  election makes the gh-1801 tolerance contract ("the loser uploads into
  the winner's release") actually true. Human (unmarked) drafts never win
  and are never touched (E1); the script is best-effort (warn + green —
  the sweeper is the backstop) except for a malformed identity, which
  fails loud like the marker-stamping scripts. Pinned by

arguments.content:
### Root Cause

The daily sweep filed gh-2372 for draft `v1.0.760` — but the release itself was published by a green train; nothing died. Inside one `build-macos.yml` run the sibling jobs (`build-macos-cli-arm64/x64`, `build-extension`) race `release_lazy_draft.sh` for the same tag; when their view→create calls interleave, **both `gh release create --draft` calls succeed** (GitHub does not enforce one release per tag for drafts) and a twin draft is born. The train publishes exactly one; the twin rots 24h+ until the sweeper deletes it and re-files the recurring issue. Evidence: v1.0.760's published object (453463937, marker `run/44870476733/job/build-extension`) and the swept twin share `created_at 2026-11-21T05:29:27Z` and the same run; v1.0.763's twin (454339915, zero assets, marker `run/45007933749/job/build-extension`) was still live when the sweep counted it "fresh: 1". No guard covered it: the failure-path guards never fire (all jobs green) and `release_draft_dedupe.sh` matches only the **train's** own-run twins — child-run twins were invisible.

### Fix

- `scripts/release_draft_twin_dedupe.sh` (new) — after a successful draft create, the creator self-deletes its OWN draft (exact `release-draft-owner` marker match, delete by id) when an older (lower id) same-tag release exists that is published or pipeline-created; the caller then attaches into the winner by tag. Deterministic election (ids are monotonic), best-effort (warn + green; the sweeper stays the backstop), human drafts never win and are never touched (E1).
- `scripts/release_lazy_draft.sh`, `scripts/release_attach_or_create.sh` — call the dedupe right after their successful creates.
- `scripts/sweep_stale_drafts.sh` — a MARKED draft whose tag already carries a published release is reclaimed immediately (fresh **or** stale) as routine hygiene (gh-236 convention: own summary/issue section, never a finding, so a residual twin can't re-file the recurring issue); the clean-sweep auto-close names twin reclaims. The misleading "a `gh release create` step died" prose can no longer fire for this shape.

### Test Coverage

- `test/release_draft_twin_dedupe_test.dart` (new, 9 tests): lazy-draft loser self-deletes its twin; winner keeps; human draft never wins/is never deleted; published-older wins; delete-blip stays green; attach-or-create path; no-op when our draft is gone; malformed identity fails loud; wiring order in both creators.
- `test/release_fresh_twin_reclaim_test.dart` (new, 5 tests): fresh/stale marked twins on a published tag reclaimed as hygiene with no issue filed; auto-close names reclaims; unpublished-tag fresh drafts untouched; unmarked author-bot drafts keep the bot-bucket finding.
- Release family: `release_hygiene`, `release_stale_draft_reclaim`, `release_lazy_draft_mint`, `release_attach_or_create_mint`, `release_draft_dedupe`, `release_flow_race`, `release_publish_immutability`, `release_empty_latest_guard`, `release_asset_gate` — all green (202 pre-existing + 14 new).
- `dart analyze` — 0 issues in touched files (repo's pre-existing 78 unrelated issues unchanged from base).

### Notes

- No workflow YAML changes: the guard lives in the two create scripts every draft-creating path already goes through.
- The live v1.0.763 twin (454339915) is intentionally left in place: the next daily sweep reclaims it as hygiene (non-finding) and the open gh-2372 issue auto-closes on the first clean sweep.
- docs/ci.md documents the new guard and sweeper behavior in the release-hygiene section.

All done. Final verification passed on every item — here is the complete report.

## Summary

**Root cause (verified against live GitHub data):** gh-2372's swept draft `v1.0.760` was not a "step died mid-publish" case — the creating run 44870476733 **succeeded**. Inside one `build-macos.yml` run, sibling jobs (`build-macos-cli-arm64/x64`, `build-extension`) race `release_lazy_draft.sh` for the same tag; when their view→create calls interleave (production: the same second), **both `gh release create --draft` calls succeed** (GitHub permits multiple drafts per tag) and a twin draft is born. The tag train publishes one; the twin rots 24h+ and re-files the recurring sweep issue. Proof: v1.0.760's published object (id 453463937, marker `run/44870476733/job/build-extension`) and the swept twin share `created_at 2026-11-21T05:29:27Z` + the same run; v1.0.763's twin (id 454339915, zero assets, marker `run/45007933749/job/build-extension`) was still live. No guard covered child-run twins on a green train: failure-path guards never fire, and `release_draft_dedupe.sh` matches only the **train's** own-run twins (its log said "no own-run twin drafts" for v1.0.760).

**Fix (two layers, per issue #282's lifecycle invariant):**
- `scripts/release_draft_twin_dedupe.sh` (new) — after a successful draft create, self-delete OUR draft (exact marker match, delete by id) when an older (lower id) same-tag release is published or pipeline-created; deterministic election, best-effort, humans never touched (E1). Wired into `release_lazy_draft.sh` + `release_attach_or_create.sh` right after their creates.
- `scripts/sweep_stale_drafts.sh` — a marked draft whose tag already carries a published release is reclaimed immediately (fresh **or** stale) as non-finding hygiene (gh-236 convention), so the misleading "a `gh release create` step died" prose can never fire for this shape again and the open issue auto-closes on the first clean sweep.
- `docs/ci.md` documents both; no workflow YAML changes needed.

**Verification:** RED-first (7 failing reproduction tests), then green; full suite `dart test --exclude-tags integration` = **14872 passed, 16 skipped** (environment-conditional); the 1-line sweeper delta that landed mid-flight re-verified by a fresh 92-test run of the sweeper/twin suites; `dart analyze` clean on touched files; the live twin- election jq validated read-only against the real roster.
